title: Company under scrutiny for ties to Nvidia and China
summary: The unusual global footprint of Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's powerful AI computer chips, is fueling questions about whether it's a front for the Chinese government.
story: The unusual global footprint of Megaspeed International, the Singapore-based company at the center of the Nvidia Chinese spy scandal, is fueling questions about whether it's a front for the Chinese government.

One of Megaspeed's leaders is Alice Huang, the woman with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was having an affair, and who is suspected by U.S. intelligence of being an asset of China's Ministry of State Security. On Thursday, Jensen Huang resigned.

In the past three years, Megaspeed, formerly a gaming company, has been one of Nvidia's biggest foreign customers, purchasing nearly $5 billion in AI chips and advanced hardware, The New York Times first reported.

And yet Megaspeed's corporate headquarters sat practically empty, according to The Straits Times, an English-language newspaper in Singapore. Questions have also been raised about its outposts in Australia and Malaysia.

Published reports in recent days revealed that the company listed a newspaper vendor as the director of its Australian subsidiary, and one of its Malaysia offices consisted of a dilapidated storefront outside Kuala Lumpur. Yet another Malaysia office was tucked into a shopping mall.

Megaspeed began as an offshoot of a China-based gaming firm and grew into a juggernaut by gaining access to restricted Nvidia AI computer chips. U.S. investigators say that Alice Huang used her contacts in the industry and a series of shell companies to gain access to 240,000 chips banned for export into China. Now it is being probed in both the U.S. and Singapore for allegedly smuggling those chips into China.

In a statement Thursday, Megaspeed said it "takes its compliance obligations under U.S. export control laws extremely seriously" and that it's "committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government."

The company also said that it "has cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and stands ready to cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority."
President Trump said this week the FBI is also investigating romantic and business ties between Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang and Alice Huang (who are not related).

Earlier this week, Jensen Huang, who is married, apologized for the affair in a statement to Nvidia's employees. The company launched an independent investigation of the matter, and an Nvidia shareholder filed a class action lawsuit Tuesday alleging that Huang concealed a relationship with Alice Huang and misled shareholders about national security concerns raised by the relationship.

Nvidia's board said Sunday that it had no reason to believe that the company's secrets or national security were compromised. "The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," its statement said.
However, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News on Wednesday that the board was preparing to oust Jensen Huang, a development that was first reported by the Wall Street Journal.

China expert Jacqueline Deal said that Nvidia's advanced AI chips could have ended up with the Chinese military. Deal, who is an adviser to State Armor, a nonprofit that studies global security threats, told CBS News, "If allegations are true, who will be fired? Nvidia has a compliance team that may have failed utterly."

She also questioned the effectiveness of the U.S. Commerce Department, which has jurisdiction over export controls that may have been bypassed, potentially giving the Chinese military access to the world's most advanced chips.
Here's what we now know about Megaspeed:

It is a major Nvidia customer. Megaspeed and its Malaysian affiliate, Speedmatrix, purchased $4.8 billion of Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence equipment and processors over the last three years.
In 2025, Megaspeed International faced an investigation by Singapore police for alleged breaches of local laws, but no details have emerged about the probe, according to The Straits Times.
The company grew rapidly.

"Megaspeed International is a premier business partner of NVIDIA, strategically positioned in the Asia Pacific region," according to its LinkedIn profile, which claims it has between 201 and 500 employees. Three years ago it listed between two and 10 employees, according to the South China Morning Post.

Megaspeed International did not reply to a request for comment. It posted an "official statement" on its website addressing what it called "misleading information" and "incorrect insinuations" accusing it of involvement in illegal chip transfers.

"We want to be absolutely clear over the past six months our company has undergone multiple on-site inspections and reviews by key institutions, including the Bureau of Industry and Security of the US Commerce Department, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry of Malaysia and NVIDIA," said the message, which also appeared on the company's LinkedIn page.
"These thorough investigations have confirmed that there has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities," the company said.

But in a statement on Thursday, the company said it had "retained a leading U.S. law firm to ... independently verify its export control compliance practices. Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws."

Megaspeed was originally incorporated in 2015 under the name 7Road International, a subsidiary of a Chinese developer of popular video games and mobile apps based in Shenzhen, China, according to corporate filings.
Huang Le Limited, a shell company in the British Virgin Islands, acquired 7Road International in March 2023. Huang Le is the Chinese name of Alice Huang.
That same month, 7Road International was renamed Megaspeed International, and Huang became its managing director. The company also launched a subsidiary called Speedmatrix.

By the end of October 2023, Huang and another Megaspeed director, Cang Yang, resigned from the company after it was bought up by a firm called Swiftdata, whose director is based in China, documents show.

But there's some indication Huang may still be affiliated with the company. Culper Research, an activist short-selling firm, published a 40-page report on Nvidia in May that cited Megaspeed employees who said Huang was still running the company.

The report also raised some concern about Jensen Huang's relationship with Megaspeed and Alice Huang, stating, "Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has not only vouched for Megaspeed, but seems to have quite literally walked alongside Megaspeed at every step, while maintaining an uncomfortably close relationship with Megaspeed's Alice Huang, a Chinese national."
Megaspeed lists its headquarters office address on the seventh floor of the Ocean Financial Centre in Singapore, a glass office tower in Singapore's central business district.

When the Straits Times and The New York Times visited the Singapore offices around the same time late last year, they found little or no staff working. The Straits Times said the door was locked, and the Times found just two people in its office on a workday.

Megaspeed has an Australian subsidiary on the 10th floor of a commercial and retail tower in the heart of Sydney's central business district. Forty other businesses are on the same floor, and space in the building can be rented for as little as $17 per day, Australia's ABC News reported. Corporate filings name Shanghai-born Kai Kang, a 29-year-old newspaper vendor, as the director, according to Australian news reports. But Kang's newsstand is in Northern Victoria, over 400 miles from Sydney. Kang's father told Australia's ABC News this week that he had never heard of Megaspeed.

title: Huang's exit rocks Nvidia and creates openings for rival firms
summary: Huang was a visionary leader with deep relationships in the complex world of tech. Losing him will hurt Nvidia, according to Wall Street analysts.
story: The abrupt resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raises questions about the strategic direction of the world's most important chipmaker and opens the door to competitors at a pivotal moment for the growing artificial intelligence business, according to technology industry experts.

"He has really created the AI revolution," Yorkville Ives and Co. tech analyst Dan Ives told CBS News. "There is no way to sugarcoat it. It's a gut punch to the industry that had so much confidence in and praise for him."

Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia effective immediately following a scandal involving an alleged spy, the company's board of directors announced Thursday. Nvidia on Thursday appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as its interim CEO, as the company launches a search for a permanent chief executive.

Yet Huang's long-range strategic vision, unique qualities as a leader and deep connections in the tech world will be hard to replace, Ives emphasized. "The biggest fear of any competitors, as well as China, is Jensen," he said. "You take him out, and it levels the playing field for domestic chipmakers and other players globally."
What does Huang's departure mean for Nvidia?

Nvidia controls roughly 90% of the market for graphics processing units, critical components for training and deploying AI models. That dominance will not suddenly evaporate because Huang is no longer at the helm, with the company's product development roadmap already anchored to a new family of chips and strong global demand for its tech, according to Ives.

"They are roughly 2-3 years ahead of the nearest competitor, and the demand trajectory the next few years is not changing because Jensen is gone," he told investors in a research note, describing Nvidia as the "clear leader in GPU chips for the AI revolution."

Cody Acree, an equity research analyst at StoneX, said the business and operational impact of Huang's ouster on Nvidia is likely to be limited over the next year or two. "Everything is already designed, planned, booked, and scheduled for production and delivery well into 2028," he told CBS News.

Yet Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, possessed other abilities that even top execs could find hard to match, according to the company's followers. Tech analysts point to his sense of timing and ability to strike partnerships and other deals, a key skill in building a global corporate powerhouse in the deeply interconnected world of tech.

"Our concern ... is that without Huang, Nvidia loses the creative, relationship-driven dealmaking that has underpinned its market leadership over the last two years," William Blair & Co. tech analyst  Sebastien Naji said in a report.

Huang was especially creative in fueling demand for Nvidia's products by financing some of its major customers, including a February deal to invest $30 billion in ChatGPT developer OpenAI, which buys Nvidia GPUs and other hardware.

"He was equally central on the supply side, securing leading allocations of memory, wafers, and optics through prepayments, multiyear purchase agreements, and equity stakes in suppliers," Naji said. "While existing contracts will survive a CEO change, what's at risk is the next round of deals, and with it Nvidia's ability to defend its share into 2027 and beyond."
Over the longer term, Huang's departure could help other AI gear manufacturers, such as AMD and Broadcom, gain ground on Nvidia, according to tech analysts.

"This presents an opportunity for some of Nvidia's competitors to take a bigger share of the market than they were planning to over the next few years," Naji said. "That happens anytime a company is distracted by an investigation, or succession planning, and takes their eye off the ball in terms of a product roadmap in a competitive space."

title: Famed Darth Vader light saber sells for almost $5 million at auction
summary: A light saber used by Darth Vader in the "Star Wars" movies "The Empire Strikes Back" and "Return of the Jedi" has sold for nearly $5 million in an auction.
story: A light saber used by Darth Vader in the "Star Wars" movies "The Empire Strikes Back" and "Return of the Jedi" sold Thursday for nearly $5 million in an auction.

The light saber, which was used in the climactic duel in Cloud City in which Vader tells Luke Skywalker "I am your father" sold for $4.875 million at the Ultimate Star Wars Auction held by Heritage Auctions. The sale marks a world auction record for any "Star Wars" collectible, according to the auction house.

The sale also established a new auction record for a screen-used "Star Wars" prop, according to the auction organizer, shooting past its $3.75 million July auction sale of Skywalker's light saber and severed hand-effects rig from "The Empire Strikes Back."

Heritage's Thursday auction also featured material from "Star Wars" Episodes I through IX and additional films and TV shows. In addition to Vader's light saber, 27 other "Star Wars" light sabers were assembled for public auction, according to Heritage Auctions.

title: FBI recovers $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance
summary: The FBI says it's seized more than $1.2 billion of cryptocurrency reported stolen last month from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.
story: Washington — The FBI said Thursday that it had seized more than $1.2 billion of cryptocurrency reported stolen last month from Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange.
The theft of about $6.3 billion from Binance is regarded as the biggest crypto heist in history, and the FBI has previously attributed it to a North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor.

The U.S. government and private sector have so far combined to freeze more than $2.7 billion of the stolen funds, and the Justice Department said Thursday that it has now obtained court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of that total.
Typically in those situations, the U.S. government will file a claim of forfeiture with a judge, who will then determine who has a legitimate claim to the recovered funds.

Also Thursday, the FBI blamed North Korea for a separate social engineering scheme that officials say resulted in the theft of $400 million worth of cryptocurrency over the last 18 months. That scheme, known as FaceStealer, involves a complicated chain of events combining the hijacking of popular messaging apps and the recording of deepfake videos.
U.S. officials have repeatedly accused North Korea of using cyber schemes to generate funds for its regime, including its illicit weapons program.

"Cryptocurrency unfortunately has become fertile ground for North Korea to defraud victims and fund its malign activities," First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California Bill Essayli said in a Justice Department statement. "Today's seizure shows that America will continue the fight against rogue states who financially gain from cybercrime."

U.S. Attorney for D.C. Jeanine Pirro said in the statement that "By springing into action at a moment's notice, we worked together to freeze this massive criminal fraud in its tracks. The North Korean regime may think they are sophisticated cyber criminals, but we have consistently met them head on, as we did here seizing more than $1.2 billion of their stolen assets."

title: USPS adds permanent postage surcharge, citing higher fuel costs
summary: Still swimming in red ink, the USPS said it will raise some postage prices in 2027 to offset elevated fuel costs.
story: The U.S. Postal Service on Thursday said it will permanently raise postage rates next year to cover higher fuel costs.

The USPS will make a temporary 8% surcharge on select postage prices, originally introduced in April, permanent in 2027, and also tack on a 3% price increase. The USPS Board of Governors, which oversees the agency's policies, approved the 11% hike, according to the USPS.
The changes will take effect on Jan. 17, 2027.

"The USPS governors believe these new rates will keep the Postal Service competitive while providing the agency with much needed revenue as it continues to struggle with financial issues," the agency said in a statement.
The agency will reevaluate the surcharge in July 2027 based on fuel prices in the first half of the year.
The USPS also said it would increase domestic shipping service costs by an average of 5.9% for Priority Mail service, Priority Mail Express, USPS Ground Advantage and Parcel Select.

In addition, international rates will rise by an average of 7.9% for Priority Mail Express International, Priority Mail International, First-Class Package International Service and International Priority Airmail.

Like other shipping and delivery companies, the USPS has faced sharply higher costs this year due to soaring diesel prices, which have spiked alongside global oil costs driven up by the war in Iran. The national average price of diesel was $6.10 per gallon on Thursday, up from $3.76 a year ago, according to AAA.

The USPS, which is self-financed, has for years struggled with high costs and dwindling mail volume. The agency on Tuesday reported a $6.5 billion loss for fiscal year 2026, down from a $9 billion loss last year. To stanch the bleeding, the Postal Service has implemented a 10-year plan to reduce expenses and restore profitability.

The U.S. Postal Service was established in 1775, with Benjamin Franklin serving as the first postmaster general. As an independent agency, the Postal Service is run by the USPS Board of Governors, which includes the postmaster general and a deputy postmaster general.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns in wake of affair, spy scandal
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned effective immediately, the company's board of directors announced Thursday.
story: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of AI tech giant Nvidia effective immediately following a scandal involving an alleged spy, the company's board of directors announced Thursday.

The decision came amid an investigation into Huang's affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspect was spying for China. President Trump said this week the FBI is investigating romantic and business ties between Huang and suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang. The two aren't related.
Nvidia's board had been preparing to oust Huang, two sources familiar with the matter confirmed to CBS News on Wednesday night, plans that were first reported by the Wall Street Journal.

Huang's ouster also follows a New York Times report Wednesday that five employees at Nvidia came forward alleging Huang was romantically involved with a subordinate, Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare.

The Times also reported Huang and Powell, who are both married to other people, were caught on video being affectionate at a conference in March, according to two Nvidia employees. The Times has not seen the video and CBS News has not verified the report.

After Huang's resignation was announced Thursday, the Reuters news agency reported that Huang also had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter. The agency only identified the employee as a woman.
The company's interim CEO will be Colette Kress, who is currently Nvidia's chief financial officer and will continue in that role.

"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," Harvey Jones, who was announced as the company's first board chair, said in a statement.
Kress has been Nvidia's CFO since she joined the company in 2013. She previously worked in finance roles at tech companies like Cisco and Microsoft for nearly 25 years.

Nvidia was co-founded by Huang in 1993. It became one of the most valuable companies in the world by designing the powerful semiconductors that fuel many of the world's leading AI firms, making its technology highly sensitive and subject to export controls limiting sales to China.
Nvidia's stock plunged as news emerged of the company's turmoil, potentially erasing almost $500 billion in value. In Thursday's trading, the stock price closed down 4.3% at $166.19.
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was an executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data center company whose website touts its partnership with Nvidia.

Megaspeed grew with the help of access to Nvidia's restricted AI computer chips. According to U.S. investigators, Alice Huang was able to gain access to 240,000 chips that were banned from being exported to China. Megaspeed is under investigation in the U.S. and Singapore for allegedly smuggling those chips into China.
In Washington, top Democrats on Capitol Hill have expressed concerns over whether Jensen Huang's ties to Alice Huang may have compromised U.S. national security.
Following Jensen Huang's resignation, Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts said his departure doesn't absolve him or the company from the scandal.
"Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and NVIDIA's board of directors still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Warren said in a statement.
Before Huang resigned, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., told CBS News the departure could help China in the competition between Beijing and the U.S.

"With him out as CEO, China could significantly narrow the gap versus the U.S.," Ives said. He added: "The problem now is that there's no replacement for Jensen. It's a black eye moment for him, for Nvidia, and actually the U.S. tech industry. I'd say it's dark day for, you know, U.S. technology."
Following Thursday morning's announcement, Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social platform that there was "only one man" who could replace Huang: former Apple CEO Tim Cook.

Mr. Trump had a close relationship with Huang, who has attended AI-focused White House events and traveled with Mr. Trump to China. Late last year, Mr. Trump granted Nvidia the right to sell advanced H200 chips to "approved customers" in China, with the U.S. government getting a 25% cut — a major coup for Huang, who has long sought to sell more technology to the Chinese market. The deal did not cover Nvidia's even more advanced Blackwell and Rubin systems.

In a radio interview Thursday, Mr. Trump brought up that he gave Huang a National Medal of Science earlier this year. "What a horrible thing that is," he said of the situation involving Huang, adding, "That's so sad to see that happen."
The president also said in an interview: "What a horrible thing that is
In a statement accompanying her appointment as interim CEO, Kress said that the company's focus will be on "serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders."

"NVIDIA's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years," Kress said.
The board said it will be conducting a search for a permanent CEO and will consider internal and external candidates.

title: Nvidia sheds almost $500 billion in value as Jensen Huang resigns
summary: Shares of the chipmaker extended their losses after Nvidia said its longtime CEO is stepping down amid revelations of a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
story: The shock resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday renewed pressure on the chipmaker's shares, with the company shedding almost $500 billion in value since the close of U.S. trading last week.
Nvidia announced Huang's resignation on Thursday morning. In a statement, the company said Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO.
Nvidia shares fell $7.54, or 4.3%, to $166.19, paring its losses after tumbling as much as 14.3% earlier in the day.

The latest drop comes after the stock shed 9.6% of its value in trading on Monday and Tuesday following the disclosure last weekend that Huang had an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe was a Chinese asset.

Nvidia, co-founded by Huang in 1993, became a key player in artificial intelligence due to its powerful semiconductors that fuel many of the world's leading AI firms. Because of Nvidia's importance to the growing industry, its chips are subject to export controls that limit their sales to China. Huang had pushed the Trump administration to relax some of those regulations.

Huang, one of the world's best-known CEOs, has served as the face of the AI industry, promoting its benefits and arguing that new regulations weren't necessary to ensure its safety. Before this week's revelations about his relationship with Chinese business executive Alice Huang (no relation), he had been seen as essential to Nvidia's success, with Wall Street analysts warning that the stock could plunge if he were ousted or resigned.
Separately, The New York Times reported Thursday that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, citing other company employees.

Huang's "value to the company pre and post this week is dramatically different, and the board did what we said it needed to do, which is rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him after this dark moment for Jensen and Nvidia," said Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives in a Thursday research note.
In a separate report, Ives estimated Nvidia's value at $225 per share if Huang left the company, compared with $300 per share if he remained at the helm.
"There is no credible way to put a precise revenue loss on his departure," said Ipek Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote.
"Customers buy Nvidia's computing power, software and networking ecosystem, and those advantages wouldn't disappear with its CEO," she said.

Nvidia's woes also come at a sensitive time for the AI industry, which has already faced investor concerns about a potential slowdown. Among the questions facing the sector is whether it will prove profitable enough to justify massive investments in the technology.
Anthropic's initial public offering will provide another key test, with the Claude AI bot developer expected to make its market debut as early as next week.

title: Who will succeed Jensen Huang at Nvidia? Analysts weigh in.
summary: Analysts say the board will be on the hunt for someone who has the technological know-how to lead the world's leading chip manufacturer.
story: Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation on Thursday as Nvidia's CEO leaves the chipmaker searching for a successor who can replace an executive synonymous with the artificial intelligence boom and who is credited with transforming the company into a $4 trillion behemoth.

The board's announcement of Huang's departure said that Colette Kress, the company's chief financial officer, will serve as interim CEO until it selects a permanent replacement. The board "will consider internal and external candidates," the statement said.

Jensen, 63, had led Nvidia since co-founding the business more than three decades ago, but stepped down following reports of his relationship with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy. The CEO had more than 60 direct reports, giving him extraordinary control over the company's decisions.
His resignation leaves a major leadership vacuum for a company that's responsible for supplying nearly the entire market share of chips needed to power frontier artificial intelligence models.

"The trouble is, I don't know that you can find anyone within Nvidia that has the sort of purview that Jensen has," Patrick McGee, a contributing writer for the Free Press and author of the book "Apple in China: The Capture of the World's Greatest Company," told CBS News on Thursday. "I mean, this was an organization set up for him to run the next 20 years, as he said in the summer."

Nvidia's board is expected to take its time choosing Huang's successor, who will lead the world's second-most valuable company by market capitalization. Finding an executive with both the engineering and leadership skills to replace Huang could require an extensive search, experts said.
"If they name somebody quickly, I think it'd be a mistake," Cody Acree, a senior semiconductor research analyst at StoneX, a financial services company, told CBS News.

While Wall Street analysts told CBS News that Kress is a solid choice for interim CEO, they don't believe she'll be selected as a permanent replacement for Huang. Even so, prediction markets are giving Kress a roughly one-in-five chance of succeeding Huang.

"We expect a more comprehensive search that will include internal and external candidates and that Ms. Kress will only serve on an interim basis," Gil Luria, managing director of the investment bank D.A. Davidson & Co., said in an email.
As the board deliberates, Wall Street analysts and traders on prediction-market platforms are throwing out names of possible successors. Here are some of the people who have surfaced so far.
Tim Cook, Apple executive chairman
Among the top external candidates to replace Huang is Tim Cook, Apple's executive chairman. Cook served as Apple CEO for 15 years before stepping down in September of this year.
"Tim Cook is the one that checks every box," Yorkville Ives tech analyst Dan Ives told CBS News.
President Trump endorsed Cook for the job in a Truth Social post on Thursday, calling him a legend.
"NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple," Mr. Trump wrote.
If selected, Cook, 66, would have to step down from Apple, a company he's worked at for nearly 30 years, due to possible conflicts of interest.
Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks
The CEO of the multinational cybersecurity company is another possible contender, Ives told CBS News in an email.
Arora's career has spanned multiple decades and includes stints at Google, SoftBank Group Corp,  a Japanese multinational investment holding company, and T-Mobile.
Arora recently commented on how hard it is to find compute in today's world and the central role Nvidia plays in supplying chips.

"You can make any plans you want, but those plans are, you know, you talk to Jensen, he can't give you chips till 2028," he said last month on the "All-in" podcast hosted by venture capitalists, including David Sacks, a key adviser to President Trump on technology.
Ian Buck, Nvidia computing executive
Bret Kenwell, an investment analyst at eToro, told CBS News the board will likely want a technology leader to lead the company.
That could lead them to consider Ian Buck, an Nvidia executive who currently serves as the vice president of the company's data center unit, he said.
Acree agreed, telling CBS News, "Ian makes the most sense internally."

Buck, who oversees Nvidia's AI hardware and software products, joined the company in 2004, according to his company profile. He invented CUDA, Nvidia's software platform that lets developers use its graphics chips for tasks such as training AI models, making him an integral part of the company's technological advancement.
"I imagine they'll want to keep that innovative, product/technology-type leader at the top," Kenwell told CBS News in a text message.
Johny Srouji, Apple's chief hardware officer
Tim Cook is not the only Apple employee seen as a contender for the role. McGee told CBS News on Wednesday that his bet is on Apple's chief hardware officer, Johny Srouji.

"I could see him wanting that role," McGee said. "He's someone that's been floated. But you're not going to be able to get someone with that caliber in, you know, a 72-hour period, maybe even a 12-hour period."
Semafor on Wednesday reported that Srouji is among the replacements the board is considering, citing a person familiar with the matter.
Rene Haas, CEO of Arm
Rene Haas, the CEO of Arm, a British semiconductor manufacturing company, is another name floated by analysts.

Acree said Haas has a solid grasp of the chip industry, something the board will be seeking out as it considers candidates. He's also a former Nvidia employee, working as the vice president and general manager of its computing products business before joining Arm in 2013.
"It's not a perfect fit by any means, but he definitely has the design expertise to run a technical organization like Nvidia," he told CBS News.
What do the prediction markets say?
On Thursday morning, prediction market users were placing bets on who Nvidia might tap as its long-term CEO.

On Kalshi's "Who will be the next CEO of Nvidia" market, Ian Buck was the top contender as of Thursday afternoon, with traders putting the chances he'll be selected as the next leader at 42%. Colette Kress has a 12% chance, and Apple's Johny Srouji is at 9%, according to Kalshi bets.

title: Here's how Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation unfolded at Nvidia
summary: Jensen Huang's shocking exit as CEO of Nvidia unspooled suddenly, yet signs of trouble had emerged much earlier.
story: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia caps a tumultuous week for the chipmaker, with his resignation coming less than a week after his extramarital relationship with a suspected Chinese spy became public.

But the seeds for Huang's downfall were planted much earlier. The woman with whom he had a relationship, Alice Huang (no relation), arrived on the tech scene in 2023, when she became the managing director of Singapore-based data center Megaspeed International.

Megaspeed, which on Thursday said it has complied with U.S. laws, would proceed to buy billions of dollars in Nvidia chips and servers. Over the past two years, Alice Huang, also known by her Chinese name Huang Le, has been photographed and recorded socializing with Jensen Huang, prompting questions in May from one quizzical investor about their "uncomfortably close relationship."
Below is a timeline of events that led to Huang's startling resignation on Thursday.
November 2015

Alice Huang, a former television reporter in China, joins investment firm Shanghai Hexi Investment Management as deputy general manager, according to social media posts and records from Simuwang, a Chinese private equity database. Shanghai Hexi was founded by Kang Wei, who became her husband, according to the Wall Street Journal.
March 2023

7Road International, originally incorporated in Singapore in 2015 as 7Road International, is renamed Megaspeed, and ownership of the "neocloud" company is transferred to Huang Le Ltd., an enterprise controlled by Alice Huang. She becomes its managing director.
June 2023
Cloud-computing company Shanghai Century Litong is founded. A company linked to Alice's sister, Huang Yu, held an ownership stake.
October 2023
Nvidia designates Shanghai Century Litong as a preferred cloud partner, giving the Chinese company priority access to Nvidia's chips, according to The Information.
Around November 2023
Megaspeed's shares were transferred to another Singapore company, Swiftdata, and Alice Huang ceased to be listed as a director of the company, according to news site Caixin Global.
June 7, 2024
Information technology firm NetThunder posted a picture on social media of Alice Huang and Jensen Huang with other tech executives at a bar in Taipei, Taiwan.
End of 2024
Megaspeed's assets exploded from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024, according to financial filings reviewed by Reuters.

Shipment records from December 2024 through early 2026, analyzed by short-selling firm Culper Research, suggest that Megaspeed's Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix, imported about $4 billion in products from a company that builds equipment with Nvidia chips.
Early 2025

Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, jointly pitched Chinese investors on a Southeast Asia data center project, reportedly telling them they had "no problem securing GPUs" — the graphics processing units Nvidia specializes in — and citing Alibaba as a customer, according to the Financial Times.
January 31, 2025
Jensen Huang meets with President Trump at the White House. It marks their first of many White House encounters in Mr. Trump's second term.
February 2025
Singapore opens an investigation into Megaspeed and several other companies over suspected false declarations related to the purchase of servers and other offenses, according to Bloomberg News.
Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are recorded on video together at a dinner at San Liu Shi Fu restaurant in Taipei, around the time of the Computex tech conference in Taiwan.
July 2025

Jensen Huang says the technology giant has won approval from the Trump administration to sell its advanced H20 computer chips, used to develop artificial intelligence, to China, a reversal of prior administration policy.
"It's so innovative and dynamic here in China that it's really important that American companies are able to compete and serve the market here in China," Huang said at the time.
That same month, Nvidia becomes the first public company to be worth $4 trillion.
February 2026
Chinese police detained Kang Wei, Alice Huang's husband and business partner, in connection with suspected stock manipulation, sources told Caixin.

That same month, Singapore barred Alice Huang from re-entering the country after she downplayed her role at Megaspeed amid the country's investigation into its operations, according to a Bloomberg News report.
Jensen Huang boards Air Force One in Alaska to accompany Mr. Trump on a two-day trip to Beijing.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio briefed Mr. Trump about the counterintelligence risk posed by Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang, according to the New York Times. The briefing, which occurred before Jensen Huang joined the trip, was the second briefing Mr. Trump had received from U.S. intelligence about the Nvidia CEO's relationship, the Times reported.
September 24, 2026
Jensen Huang attends Mr. Trump's state dinner for China's Xi Jinping at the White House.
September 29, 2026
Jensen Huang attends an AI event at the White House and signs a set of voluntary AI safety standards amid calls for tighter guardrails on the technology.
November 8, 2026

Jensen Huang writes a message to Nvidia employees admitting that he had an extramarital affair. The same day, Nvidia's board said it had launched an independent investigation amid reports that its CEO was the target of a "foreign intelligence effort."
The New York Times on Nov. 8 reported that U.S. government surveillance suggested Alice Huang was feeding information directly to Beijing.
November 9, 2026

At an impromptu press conference at the White House, Mr. Trump said he had spoken to Jensen Huang and that the tech exec had indicated he was unaware of Alice Huang's links to China's intelligence services. Mr. Trump also described the Nvidia CEO as an "honorable man" who's "definitely suffering."
Mr. Trump didn't address questions about when he first learned about the spy allegations, only saying, "not too long ago" and that "it didn't make much of an impact on me."
November 11, 2026
The New York Times reports that Jensen Huang had an affair with Kimberly Powell, a subordinate at Nvidia.
November 12, 2026
Nvidia's board of directors announces that Jensen Huang has resigned, effective immediately.

title: While many Americans resist, China embraces AI data center boom
summary: Far from the opposition American tech giants face, it's smooth sailing for the Chinese AI firms racing to catch up, and hoping to overtake them.
story: Ulanqab, China — Off a major highway on the outskirts of Ulanqab, in the Chinese province of Inner Mongolia, Hereford cows roam through corn fields scouring the ground for any dried up remains of the recent harvest.

Hovering over the landscape are shiny new transmission towers linked by power cables that stretch along the plateau for as far as the eye can see. On the ridgeline, covered in snow, wind turbines spin, taking full advantage of the ever-blowing wind.

The energy pulsing from the remote Chinese region — a combination of renewables and fossil fuels — will soon power multi-story data centers being constructed on farmland as part of a sprawling AI data center construction boom.
The construction site is the size of a small American city. It is the biggest, and fastest growing infrastructure project anywhere in China right now.

This corner of Inner Mongolia was famous for generations for growing potatoes. Now, it's fast becoming an AI hub, and Chinese officials hope the expansive, rugged landscape will help power the country's ambition to surpass the U.S. as the global leader in artificial intelligence.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns in wake of affair, China spy scandal
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns in wake of affair, China spy scandal
Baletu, a 72-year-old farmer, who has lived here for more than 40 years growing potatoes and corn, said the changes across his local landscape are positive.
"It doesn't affect my farmland, not at all," he told CBS News. "It's good for the area."

A short drive away, CBS News was able to see what all that wind power will soon be feeding. Trucks, cranes and thousands of workers are taking part in the construction project to create one of the biggest data centers anywhere in the world.

We drove miles down new roads with multistory data centers going up on either side. Even from the road it was easy to spot the countless racks that will hold servers, semi-conductor chips and cooling and exhaust fans.

There are dozens of data centers being built in Inner Mongolia, more than any other part of the vast nation. The reason they have chosen Ulanqab is because it offers cheap, abundant energy. Fossil fuels are still the main source of power here, but they also use renewables, including wind and solar.

Ulanqab is one of the most consistently windy locations in the province. The climate is also cold all year, which helps keep cooling costs down, and land and labor are more affordable in the remote region.
Experts cited by the Financial Times say data centers in China are built at about one-fifth of the costs incurred in the U.S., not least due to the much higher land and labor costs.

As many as 30,000 workers have been brought in from across China to help build the AI hub, and in a country experiencing an economic downturn and high youth unemployment, these mass infrastructure projects are very much welcome.

"Development is the best thing, especially when it provides job opportunities for many young people," a local businesswoman who sets up a lunchtime food stall outside the construction site told CBS News.

While data centers in the U.S. face major community opposition, which could be emboldened by the "blue wave" of the Democrats' stunning midterm election performance, there are few hurdles for Chinese developers.

While China's government doesn't generally tolerate protests of any kind, and it tightly controls messaging across all media, a United Nations survey last year found that as many as 80% of people in the country support data center construction. At least two-thirds of Chinese people use AI in their day-to-day life, as many embrace the technology and the infrastructure behind it.
Under President Xi Jinping, AI development has become a national strategic priority for China.

"There is no opposition to data centers in China. It's never heard of, whereas in the U.S., it has become a huge movement against data center building in neighborhoods," Henry Wang, founder and president of the Center For China and Globalization, told CBS News.

Huawei, Alibaba, Byte Dance, Deepseek, Baidu, Z.ai, ZData and VNET — China's biggest AI companies — are all active in Inner Mongolia. In areas where construction has finished, fences are up and grounds are landscaped, and avenues through the humming data centers have been named after the AI tech giants.
While Chinese firms' AI models are believed to be about six months behind their U.S. competitors, due largely to restrictions on the sale of high-end microchips, the gap is narrowing.
China has more than double the power generation capacity of the U.S., and some experts believe access to power, not chips, will ultimately be the deciding factor in the global race for AI dominance.
"Chips may not become the latest diving criteria," said Wang. "It may be that power is the bottleneck, and whoever goes through that first gets the advantage. And right now. China has the edge."

title: China fines a company over a Dove chocolate "situationship" ad
summary: China has fined a company what amounts to about $120,000 over an ad it created for Dove chocolate featuring a woman in a "situationship," saying it promoted the "wrong views on marriage and relationships."
story: Chinese authorities have fined a company the equivalent of about $120,000 over an advertisement it created for American chocolate brand Dove that featured a woman in a "situationship," saying on Thursday it promoted the "wrong views on marriage and relationships."
The video, first posted online in August, showed a woman getting chocolates from a man with whom she was in a "situationship" after her boyfriend ignored her.
The clip caused a stir online in China, with some social media users saying it promoted infidelity, prompting Dove to issue an apology.

Zongzheng Food — the company that created the ad and that operates a Dove store on Chinese e-commerce platform Kuaishou — was fined 800,000 yuan ($120,000) last month, Shanghai authorities said on Thursday.

The ad "packaged being unfaithful in a relationship as a 'sweet experience,' promoting wrong views on marriage and relationships and violating good social customs," the Shanghai Municipal Market Supervision Administration said in a statement.
China is facing a demographic crisis after its birth rate halved over the past decade, and in response authorities have heavily promoted traditional family structures.
Marriage registrations from January to September were down 9.8% year-over-year, reaching just 4.6 million, data from China's civil affairs ministry showed last week.
Dove, which is owned by McLean, Virginia-based Mars Inc., said in its apology in August that the ad didn't follow its content review process and was "clearly inappropriate."
Dove "bears responsibility" for all content posted to its official channels, the chocolate brand said on social media platform Weibo.
Chinese authorities have previously rebuked companies for platforming romantic relationships deemed inappropriate.
In May, Chinese consumer electronics company OPPO said it "severely punished" multiple executives over an ad joking about infidelity, which authorities publicly condemned.

title: Nvidia's board preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, sources say
summary: Nvidia's board of directors is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang soon, according to two sources, amid allegations Huang had an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe was a Chinese asset.
story: Update: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned, the company's board announced. Read the latest here. Our earlier coverage is below.

Nvidia's board of directors is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang soon, according to two sources familiar with the matter, following allegations that Huang had an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe was a Chinese asset.
The Trump administration is aware of the matter, the sources said.
The Wall Street Journal was first to report on the board's moves.
Nvidia's share price slid more than 8% in after-hours trading Wednesday after the Journal's report, extending a multi-day sell-off for one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies.
The company has faced days of turmoil following reports that American intelligence agencies believed Huang was the target of a Chinese spying plot.

Nvidia was co-founded by Huang in 1993, and for years it was best known for designing graphics cards widely used for gaming. The company now designs the powerful semiconductors that fuel many of the world's leading AI firms, making its technology highly sensitive and subject to export controls limiting sales to China.

The New York Times reported last week on allegations that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, who previously led a Singapore-based firm called Megaspeed International that bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips and hardware. U.S. intelligence agencies have believed for months that Alice Huang — who is not related to Jensen Huang — was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, the newspaper reported.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday night that Alice Huang had returned to China, her home country, citing people familiar with the matter. She is living in Beijing with the knowledge of Chinese security officials, one of the people told Bloomberg, which said it wasn't immediately clear when or why she went there.
Asked Thursday about the report that Alice Huang had returned, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told reporters: "I do not have information on what you mentioned."

Separately, The New York Times reported Thursday that Jensen Huang had an additional affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, according to five people who also worked there. She reports to Huang. Both are married to other people.Huang, Powell and Nvidia have not commented on the Times report.
In a message to Nvidia employees over the weekend, Jensen Huang wrote that he was "unfaithful to my wife" and apologized for hurting her and their children.

Nvidia's board said Sunday it had launched an independent investigation into allegations that the CEO "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." The board said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised. Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said, "We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the U.S. government would have notified us."

Two law enforcement sources told CBS News the Justice Department is also investigating Megaspeed over potential violations of U.S. export restrictions on advanced AI chips. Some analysts have raised questions about whether the saga resulted in China — which is racing the U.S. for AI dominance — gaining access to Nvidia's technology through Megaspeed.

The company has denied any involvement in illegal chip transfers but said in a statement Thursday that it "retained a leading U.S. law firm to ... independently verify its export control compliance practices. Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws."

China has denied all allegations, with Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun telling reporters on Monday that the "so-called Chinese spy narrative is entirely baseless and constitutes slander and smear."

Beyond the national security concerns, Nvidia is facing a securities lawsuit accusing the company of failing to disclose information to shareholders about Jensen Huang's relationship with the alleged spy.

Jensen Huang has a close relationship with the Trump administration. President Trump gave Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 computer chips to "approved customers" in China late last year, with the federal government taking a 25% cut of chip sales. The deal did not include Nvidia's more advanced Blackwell or Rubin systems.
The Nvidia CEO and other U.S. tech executives traveled to China with Mr. Trump earlier this year.

On Monday, Mr. Trump called Jensen Huang a "very high-quality person," saying during a White House briefing that "the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape." The president said he spoke to Jensen Huang to see how he was doing, and the executive "said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy."

title: Nvidia's stock dives as board weighs move to oust Jensen Huang
summary: Nvidia shares fall sharply in after-hours trading as the company's board considers whether to remove Jensen Huang as CEO.
story: Nvidia's stock price tumbled after the close of trading on Wednesday on news that the chipmaker's board of directors is preparing to oust longtime CEO Jensen Huang.

Nvidia this week launched an investigation into Huang, who admitted to having an extramarital affair. U.S. intelligence agencies have linked the CEO to a Chinese business executive, Alice Huang (no relation), who is suspected of being an asset of China's Ministry of State Security.
The Trump administration is aware of the Nvidia board's plans, sources told CBS News. The Wall Street Journal was the first to report that board members were preparing to remove Jensen Huang.

Nvidia shares fell more than 8%, to $159.51, in after-hours trading. The drop continued a steep decline in the company's market value, which has sunk more than $450 billion since Nvidia announced the probe into Jensen Huang's conduct on Nov. 8.

Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, is seen in many circles as the face of the burgeoning artificial intelligence sector, with the company's advanced chips providing the critical computing resources that power frontier AI models.
His departure would be a major blow to Nvidia, which lacks any obvious successor to fill his shoes, according to Wall Street analysts.

"The news is obviously negative, as Jensen is (arguably) the most prominent executive at the most prominent company sitting at the center of the world's most important industry — someone who foresaw the rise of AI years before ChatGPT arrived and made sure the firm he founded would be prepared to capitalize on it," Adam Crisafulli of Vital Knowledge said in a report.
Nvidia's code of conduct

Corporate governance experts said Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang appears to violate Nvidia's code of conduct. That policy highlights that personal relationships could create a conflict of interest for Nvidia, while Huang himself specifies in the code of conduct that the company's workers have a responsibility "to maintain high ethical standards."

Nvidia's code also instructs employees to ask themselves whether they could defend an action if it were made public on social media or known to colleagues. If not, the policy states, "do not proceed."

In a message to company employees on Sunday, Huang admitted to having an affair, and he apologized to his wife and their two children, both of whom also work at Nvidia. "There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," he wrote.
Nvidia's 11-person board includes Jensen Huang, although the other board members are designated as independent, according to a regulatory filing.

President Trump said this week the FBI is also investigating romantic and business ties between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who was a senior executive at Megaspeed International. The Singapore-based company has been one of Nvidia's largest foreign customers, purchasing nearly $5 billion in AI chips and other advanced hardware.
The turmoil at Nvidia is also drawing scrutiny in Congress, with lawmakers expected to question company executives about whether its chips are being funneled to China through other countries.

Dan Ives, a tech analyst with investment adviser Yorkville Ives, said investors will now consider who might succeed Huang, what impact that could have on the company's short-term strategy and what any government investigations might reveal.

"Jensen is not replaceable by another CEO or group of interim executives, but Nvidia likely now has to move on without Jensen at the helm, which seemed like a Twilight Zone episode narrative before Sunday afternoon when the news broke," Ives said in a report.

title: SNAP proposal would increase food insecurity, critics say
summary: Anti-hunger advocates are blasting a proposed change to SNAP rules that could cut off more than 6 million people from access to federal food aid.
story: Anti-hunger advocates are denouncing a Trump administration proposal that would tighten eligibility requirements for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).

The proposed rule, introduced on Tuesday by the U.S. Department of Agriculture to seek public comment, would change a policy that extends eligibility for SNAP to people who receive benefits through a social safety net program known as Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, or TANF.
If adopted, the SNAP rule would reduce public enrollment in the program by roughly 17%, the Agriculture Department projects.
White House spokeswoman Allison Schuster said the Trump administration wants to ensure that SNAP serves only "eligible Americans who need it most."

"Rather than throwing money at a broken system, the Trump Administration will continue to stop fraudsters stealing from these important programs, as well as take effective, cost-saving steps to make life more affordable for all Americans," she told CBS News in an email.
Broad push to narrow SNAP
Cutting off so many Americans from food stamps would greatly increase food insecurity at a time when many people are already struggling financially, critics said.

"Instead of listening to the public sentiment on affordability following the election, the administration is continuing its attacks on vital food assistance and the families who need help to put food on the table," Ty Jones Cox, vice president for food assistance at the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, a nonpartisan think tank, said in a statement.

Some lawmakers also decried the proposed rule. In a statement, Rep. Angie Craig, a Democrat from Minnesota and ranking member of the House Agriculture Committee, called the proposal "heartless and cruel."

The proposal comes amid what advocates say is a broader push by the Trump administration to narrow eligibility for food stamps. The "One Big Beautiful Bill" expanded SNAP's work requirements. As of Oct. 1, states are also required to shoulder a larger share of the cost of administering SNAP, a change advocates say could lead to further benefit cuts.
According to USDA figures, more than 5 million Americans have lost access to food stamps since the "Big Beautiful Bill" was enacted in July 2025.

"Basically, what the administration is doing is continuing on this path of making sure that SNAP is dismantled," said Gina Plata-Nino, SNAP director for the Food Research and Action Center, a nonprofit advocacy group. "The states have so much on their plate that they cannot continue running the program."

Plata-Nino said the Trump administration's changes to SNAP have created additional barriers as hunger in the U.S. is becoming more pervasive. Food insecurity has surged since the pandemic, according to research from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York earlier this year.
"We do know that in terms of hunger, it is going to raise our negative health outcomes," Plata-Nino said of the proposed SNAP rule.
What would the proposed rule do?

The latest SNAP reform proposal would restrict what's known as "broad-based categorical eligibility," a policy offered by more than 40 states that allows households outside the normal SNAP eligibility income threshold to qualify for food stamps if they receive benefits through TANF.
Plata-Nino noted that the longstanding policy authorized by Congress makes SNAP more accessible and lowers costs for states administering the program.

Under the new rule, which would take effect in 2029, households above SNAP's income thresholds would not qualify for food stamps if they receive non-cash TANF benefits, such as childcare assistance or job training.
The Trump administration issued a similar proposal in 2019, but the Biden administration withdrew it two years later.
In the text of the rule, the USDA said the current SNAP eligibility standards mean that even households with $1 million in wealth but no income could technically receive food stamps.

"Broad-based categorical eligibility has bloated the welfare rolls for decades," a USDA spokesperson said in an email to CBS News. "It has allowed states to take shortcuts, error rates to balloon, and those households with income and assets far above federal limits access to a benefit meant for the neediest among us. Correcting this loophole is long overdue."
Who would it impact?
In an analysis of the rule, the USDA estimated that 6.3 million people would lose access to SNAP in 2029, the year the proposal would take effect.

The rule would also impact access to other federal assistance programs for people who qualify based on their SNAP eligibility. Nearly 1.8 million children would lose access to free school lunches, while 5,500 low-income women would lose access to supplemental food aid for women and children, according to the agency.

Plata-Nino said FRAC believes those figures could underestimate the number of people who would lose food aid under the proposed rule. "We know that the impact is going to be higher," she told CBS News.

According to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, the rule would cut off SNAP benefits for people with a gross household income just above 130% of the poverty line, or about $35,500 per year for a family of three.

title: Tesla extends Cybertruck production to clear backlog, Musk says
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk originally said Tesla would wind down production​ at its Texas factory in mid-2027.
story: Tesla is extending a deadline it set to finish Cybertruck production to give the company more time to fulfill its orders, CEO Elon Musk announced Wednesday.

In a social media post, Musk said Tesla will continue to manufacture the Cybertruck through the end of summer 2027, giving the car company a few additional months to work through its backlog. Last week, Musk originally said Tesla would wind down production by mid-2027 when he broke the Cybertruck news to customers.
Days later, he revealed Tesla would have to return some customers' deposits, noting that the Cybertruck order rate "far exceeds" the electric vehicle maker's production rate.
"We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people," he said on X.
The announcement sparked backlash from some Tesla customers on social media who said they are still waiting to get their hands on the stainless-steel pickup truck.
"Like many of you, I have a 59k Cybertruck on order," one Reddit user wrote. "I've been excited for it, and I'm getting the feeling now that it may not happen."
In his X post on Wednesday, Musk said he was extending production despite it not being the best financial decision for Tesla.
"This is not the smartest move from a profit-maximizing standpoint btw, but there must be some room in this world for sentimentality or what's the point?" he wrote.

title: United bans AI agents from booking flights on behalf of travelers
summary: Using an artificial intelligence agent to make flight reservations poses security risks and could violate federal rules, according to United.
story: United Airlines said on Wednesday that it is banning artificial intelligence agents from making flight reservations on behalf of travelers, citing security risks and the possibility that such actions could violate federal rules.
Many consumers are turning to AI agents such as Meta's Muse and OpenAI's dots to complete tasks ranging from researching products and tracking down deals to making purchases.

To make an airline booking, an AI agent requires access to a customer's personal information, including credentials like payment information. United has a problem with that, saying that "sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles."

The carrier also said that using an AI agent to, for example, check in for a flight could violate federal regulations, including rules requiring travelers to verify in person that their luggage does not contain banned substances.

"As a result, United is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants," said the airline, which is updating its booking and ticketing policies to reflect the new rule.
United's new policy suggests the company wants to retain control over the customer booking process, said Henry Harteveldt, an aviation analyst at Atmosphere Research Group.

"United is saying they don't want to add yet another, and potentially even more powerful, intermediary than they already face in terms of Google search, price-comparison metasearch sites and online travel agencies," he told CBS News. "Flight searches cost airlines money, and undoubtedly United wants to avoid the expense associated with the surge of AI bot flight searches."

Other airlines are taking a different tack to the emergence of AI agents. For example, Southwest has made its flight inventory viewable to ChatGPT users, who can access the airline's website through the AI app.

United fares will continue to be bookable through flight aggregators such as Kayak, Hopper and Google Flights, Harteveldt said, adding that "consumers shouldn't find it any more difficult to find good fares on the airline."
"But by blocking the AI bots, United won't make it any easier to find its fares, either," he said.

title: Alaska elects first Democrat governor since 1998
summary: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, also known as JKT, campaigned on issues including affordability and funding of public schools
story: Alaska voters have elected a Democrat for governor for the first time since 1998, part of a national midterm elections wave that gave the party sweeping wins in state governments across the country.

Former state lawmaker Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republicans, including one endorsed by President Trump. His victory means Democrats will control the governor's office in 30 states, including several they flipped after years of Republican control in places such as Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas.

Kreiss-Tomkins, often referred to as JKT, completed a political comeback three years after leaving the state House. He traveled throughout Alaska to build his coalition and focused on affordability, advocated for full funding of public schools and called for all oil and gas producers to pay corporate income tax. He also sought a moratorium on new data centers until state lawmakers pass regulations for their development.

He said Alaska had become "broken" under eight years of outgoing Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy and needed a change. He cited among other issues a state ferry system that he said has been left in shambles, with routes to many communities cut drastically. The ferry is a key mode of transportation for southeast Alaska communities not connected by roads, some of which also have limited air service.
Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, emphasized a willingness to work across party lines and said he wanted a Cabinet with Republicans, Democrats and independents.

"If they're competent, if they're service-minded, if they're entrepreneurial, if they're problem-solvers, you're on the team. Game on," he said during a candidate forum last month. "Let's go, and let's get Alaska back on track."

Republican U.S. Sen. Lisa Murkowski, who has at times been at odds with her party, including Mr. Trump, endorsed Kreiss-Tomkins a week before the election. She said Kreiss-Tomkins "understands that governing requires listening to people with different perspectives and finding common ground to solve the problems all of us face."
Three former governors including Democrat Tony Knowles, independent Bill Walker and Republican Frank Murkowski, the senator's father, also endorsed him.

In a statement declaring victory earlier Friday, Kreiss-Tomkins said voters wanted change and "a government that works across party lines to move Alaska forward. Our administration will not waste a single day getting to work to solve problems for Alaska." He said his campaign had more than 10,000 donors.

title: Lutnick agrees to testify as Bessent blames him for chip sales
summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10, according to a U.S. official.
story: Washington — Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10, according to a U.S. official, amid intensifying scrutiny of the Commerce Department's oversight of the export of powerful AI chips following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

A growing number of Republicans are calling on Lutnick to answer questions about the Commerce Department's apparent delay in adding Singapore-based company Megaspeed International to the U.S. government's Entity List, which would have restricted the company's ability to get access to advanced AI chips.

Megaspeed was previously led by Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy who had an affair with Jensen Huang. The U.S. government suspects Megaspeed of directing advanced Nvidia chips to China, circumventing a U.S. export ban.

GOP Sen. Jim Banks of Indiana, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, told Fox News on Thursday that "we know that the Department of Commerce, Secretary Lutnick, it appears, used loopholes to allow some of these chip sales to occur even though President Trump has directed his administration and the Department of Commerce not to allow that to happen."

On Friday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent repeatedly emphasized that the Treasury Department and other parts of the executive branch had pushed for restrictions on Megaspeed, laying the blame for the delay at the feet of the Commerce Department.

"Treasury, War, [the U.S. Trade Representative] and State, they were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the Entity List for months, but Commerce has the pen," Bessent told CNBC. "And you will have to ask them about their internal processes."
Bessent declined to comment on reported tensions between himself and Lutnick. The Commerce Department did not immediately respond to CBS News' request for comment.

title: Democrats strategize on how to deliver on midterm mandate
summary: Democrats gathered in Denver this week for a conference on what comes next as they prepare to take control of Congress.
story: Democrats received the message loud and clear from the midterm elections that Americans want results, not "shallow litmus tests," as Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro put it at a conference in Denver this week. But it was evident that Democrats, who gathered at a summit on the way forward as they take control of the House and Senate next year, are still working out just how to achieve those results while President Trump is still in the White House.

Shapiro helped Democrats flip four House seats in his state, and he spoke after an election that delivered decisive majorities to Democrats in the Senate and the House. He said voters had rejected "chaos" and "corruption" and are demanding results-focused governance. Shapiro urged congressional Democrats to focus on lowering costs, building affordable housing, protecting consumers and expanding economic opportunity — and not on ideological fights.

The Pennsylvania governor, who has been mentioned as a possible 2028 presidential candidate, focused on national issues, arguing the "beginning of the mandate" from voters called for aggressive action on competition, AI, innovation and economic fairness. He advised Democrats to use their majorities to deliver a stronger "American bargain" for working families.

While some newly elected Democrats, like Sen.-elect James Talarico of Texas, have some optimism about the new Congress' ability to work with the Trump administration, others, including New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill, encouraged new members of Congress to be pragmatic in approaching dealmaking with Mr. Trump.
In his remarks Thursday, Talarico, who won his seat in a heavily Republican state, said that Democrats "must" work with President Trump because "the American people cannot wait two years for change."
"We should make the final two years of his presidency the most productive of any presidency in American history," Talarico said.
But Sherrill suggested that may be harder than it sounds.

"The art of the deal to Trump is, he figures out what you want. He leverages the you-know-what out of you and keeps taking, taking, taking and never delivers. He does not follow through on his commitments," Sherrill said of her experience in working with him as New Jersey's governor.
She told Democrats to take advantage of the power they amassed this election cycle and use it to their advantage.
"My advice to Senator Talarico is, if Trump wants to work with us, we will lay out the agenda and he can sign it," Sherrill said.
Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger, who won the governorship in 2025, the same year as Sherrill, agreed that trying to make deals with Mr. Trump may be futile.

"It is foolish to think if you ever make a deal, if you ever give anything, you give an inch to the president, there is no reason to believe—he has no track record of ever following through—that if you make a deal with President Trump, he will ever actually abide by it," Spanberger said.

Spanberger, who represented Virginia in the House before she was elected governor, offered this advice to next year's Democratic Congress: "Congress should pass bill after bill after bill that is broadly, very clearly popular, and is responsive to what folks across the country campaigned on, and send it to the president's desk. No pre-negotiations, no discussions. Eventually he'll want to do a signing ceremony. And eventually, he might sign a couple of them. And if not, then in 2028, folks say, look at these bills that passed through the House, passed through the Senate. The president didn't take action."

Despite the celebratory mood in Denver, Democratic officials repeatedly sent the message that they understand that last week's victories do not represent a long-term realignment, and there's no guarantee that the voters who supported them will continue to do so.
"This isn't a blank check," Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona said. "If anything, it is a short-term loan that we need to keep paying — or we will lose it."
