title: Device deemed ‘credible threat’ triggers evacuation around ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois
summary: A suspicious device at an ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, triggered evacuations within a one-mile radius, with local events forced to cancel as investigations continue.
story: A suspicious device at an ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, triggered evacuations within a one-mile radius, with local events forced to cancel as investigations continue.
Police and federal authorities said early Saturday that they had found a device deemed a “credible threat” and rendered it safe, without giving details as to its nature.
Searches were ongoing and the evacuation order remains in place, Peoria Chief of Police Brad Dixon told a press conference.
“We’re going to have to search the entire property,” Dixon said, referring to the BioUrja ethanol plant.
The area “has not been rendered safe,” he said. “There’s going to be an exhaustive search of the facility that has not been completed yet.”
“I don’t want to get into how many we found, where we found them,” he added, but said those living in a one-mile radius “should absolutely evacuate the area.”
Mayor of Peoria Rita Ali told NBC affiliate WEEK there was an “all hands on deck” response, saying: “A device has been identified. We know it’s a credible threat. We know it’s a bomb.”
​FBI Special Agent Ryan Presley told media that FBI personnel, along with local and state police, had determined a “suspicious package was a threat and rendered it safe.”
Congressman Eric Sorensen (D-Ill.) met with evacuees at Peoria Emanual High School on Friday night.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

“This is the designated shelter area for those that are impacted by the evacuation that’s going on just south of downtown Peoria,” he said in an update. “What we do need to make sure is that everybody’s making good decisions. If you are within the one mile radius of the chemical plant BioUrja in Peoria, you have to evacuate.”
Illinois Governor JB Pritzker urged locals to “follow directions from law enforcement and stay clear of the area.”
American Country Music Singer Jon Pardi was forced to cancel his show scheduled for Friday evening at the Peoria Civic Center.
“At the direction of the Chief of Police, tonight’s concert has been canceled due to an active local safety concern,” he posted on Instagram, adding that tickets would be refunded.
Dozer Park ballpark, home of Minor League Baseball side the Peoria Chiefs, also canceled a holiday event at the venue.

The nearby OSF HealthCare St. Francis Medical Center said it was “taking all appropriate precautions in response to the situation in downtown Peoria.” A statement said: “We will continue to monitor the situation and take any additional steps necessary to maintain a safe environment for those we serve and those who work at our facilities.”

title: Alaskans opt to stick with ranked choice voting
summary: Alaskans have decided to stick with ranked choice voting, rejecting a ballot measure that sought to repeal the system, NBC News projects.
story: Alaskans have decided to stick with ranked choice voting, rejecting a ballot measure that sought to repeal the system, NBC News projects.
The unusual voting method was in the spotlight after a controversy around a potential spoiler candidate in the state’s competitive Senate race gathered steam in the final stretch of the election.

In Alaska, candidates from all parties run on the same primary ballot, with the top four vote-getters advancing to the general election. Voters then rank those candidates in order of preference, and if no one eclipses the 50% threshold on the first ballot, the race goes to ranked choice tabulation.

The fourth-place finisher is eliminated, and their supporters are redistributed based on how voters ranked the other candidates on the ballot. The process continues until a candidate reaches a majority.
While supporters of the system say it gives more power to voters and incentivizes candidates to not only appeal to the most extreme elements of a party, critics argue it causes confusion.

One week before Election Day, The New York Times reported that Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola’s campaign was involved in recruiting a candidate with the same name as GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan to run for Senate. Peltola and her campaign have denied pushing Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher, to enter the race or being involved in his campaign.
The episode is under federal and state investigation, though a federal judge earlier this month dismissed an effort by the Trump administration to segregate ballots cast for Dan J. Sullivan.
Ranked choice voting first went into effect in Alaska in 2022, after voters approved it through a ballot measure in 2020. A similar effort to repeal it failed by fewer than 800 votes in 2024.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Open primaries and ranked-choice voting aren’t the only voting method that allow spoiler candidates. And supporters say that the method mitigates the effects by allowing voters to rank multiple candidates.
Alaska and Maine are the only states that use ranked-choice voting for statewide elections.

title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins the Alaska governor’s race
summary: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has won the Alaska governor’s race, NBC News projects, flipping control of the office from Republicans.
story: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has won the Alaska governor’s race, NBC News projects, flipping control of the office from Republicans.
Kreiss-Tomkins’ victory marks the latest gain for Democrats at the state level in this year’s elections. The party will hold 30 governorships next year after flipping control in six states.

At 37, Kreiss-Tomkins will be the youngest governor in Alaska history and next year he will be the youngest sitting governor in the country. Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state lawmaker, defeated three Republicans on the ballot to succeed term-limited GOP Gov. Mike Dunleavy.

In Alaska, the top four vote-getters in the primary regardless of party advance to the general election, where ranked choice voting is utilized. Kreiss-Tomkins secured a majority of the vote on the first ballot, so the ranked choice aspect did not come into play in the race.

Former state Sen. Tom Begich, a Democrat, had finished second in the August primary just behind Kreiss-Tomkins. But he dropped out of the race soon after to consolidate Democratic support behind Kreiss-Tomkins.

The three Republican candidates on the November ballot were Anchorage businesswoman Bernadette Wilson, former Anchorage Mayor Dave Bronson and former state Attorney General Treg Taylor. Wilson, who was backed by President Donald Trump, finished a distant second.

Kreiss-Tomkins, who often goes by JKT in the state, earned bipartisan support during his campaign. Most notably, he was endorsed by GOP Sen. Lisa Murkowski one week before Election Day. “JKT is a young Alaskan with a view and a perspective that I think Alaska needs right now — a freshness of energy, a common-sense guy who has a known ability to be working together,” Murkowski said in an interview with NBC affiliate KTUU of Anchorage.
Kreiss-Tomkins campaigned on boosting funding for public schools, lowering energy costs, expanding Medicaid and protecting Alaska’s fisheries.

He also called for a moratorium on all new data centers until the state Legislature can pass regulations, and said he would not allow direct or indirect subsidies to data centers for electricity costs.

title: Rubio urges conservatives to uplift their ideology, brushes off GOP midterm losses
summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday downplayed Republicans’ devastating losses in the midterm elections, instead telling supporters, “Politics requires more than simply winning elections.”
story: Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday downplayed Republicans’ devastating losses in the midterm elections, instead telling supporters, “Politics requires more than simply winning elections.”

“Those who believe that one setback, one defeat, one bad election spells the end of the republic should look to you as an example for inspiration,” Rubio said in his first major remarks since Election Day, given to the conservative Federalist Society at the National Lawyer’s Convention in Washington, D.C.
Rubio, whose name has been floated as a potential 2028 presidential candidate, told the audience, “Great things that last are built in decades, not election cycles.”
“There will be more victories, and there will be more defeats,” he said. “There will be more triumphs, and there will be more disappointments.”

The secretary of state urged the crowd to remember that the government “is not the only source of political power” as he emphasized the importance of still uplifting conservative ideology despite election losses.
Rubio pointed to power held by universities, the press and “the whole expanse of civil society.”
“Elections decide who holds office for a season, but elections, they do not decide by themselves what our institutions teach or what our lawyers believe,” Rubio said.
For Subscribers

He also condemned the “endless barrage of claims about America’s alleged violations of international rules and norms,” including allegations that the U.S. had violated international law when striking boats allegedly used to traffic drugs in the Caribbean Sea or over the Trump administration’s aggressive immigration enforcement policies.
Rubio also defended the U.S. capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and the continued war in Iran.

“None of this has anything to do with any real higher standard of justice. It is a function of the people who control the official organs of global governance,” Rubio said. “For this global elite, international law is not a neutral body of rules. International law is an instrument, an instrument to advance their interests under the pretense of universal principles.”
For Subscribers

Rubio denounced the United Nations and the International Criminal Court, saying, “Americans have never agreed to submit to the ICC’s authority, but that court and its allies in the global bureaucracy have appointed themselves judge and jury and executioner of the international order.”
Last month, the Trump administration imposed sweeping sanctions on the ICC as part of its campaign to dismantle the court after it announced investigations into the U.S.

Rubio on Friday also criticized “activist courts” on American soil, telling the crowd of lawyers, “The weaponization of international law is not altogether different from what we’ve seen here at home.”

“The activist courts who seek to govern by injunction, twisting the law to fit whatever their preferences happen to be at any given place or time,” he said, adding that the judges are “allies” of those who have “denounced the Constitution.”

“For these people, the fundamental purpose of the law, American law and international law alike, is to weaken the United States,” Rubio said. “It is to undermine our power as a sovereign nation to act. It is to hinder the American government’s ability to defend American interests at home and abroad.”

Rubio’s words echo repeated attacks by President Donald Trump on judges who rule against his interests. The president has also increasingly clashed with the Supreme Court, which holds a 6-3 conservative majority and includes three justices appointed to the bench by Trump.

The high court ruled against Trump this year on his tariff policies, his plan to diminish birthright citizenship, his efforts to interfere with mail-in ballots ahead of the midterm elections and his firing of a member of the Federal Reserve.
After the Supreme Court’s ruling on his tariff policies, Trump called the justices a “disgrace to our nation.”

title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented  meeting on the sidelines of APEC, officials say
summary: President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen, China’s tech hub, next week, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers.
story: President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen, China’s tech hub, next week, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers.

“President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the president of the United States, the president of the People’s Republic of China and the president of the Russian Federation,” Olivia Wales, a White House spokesperson, said in a call with reporters Friday night. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous.”

It is not anticipated that any sort of agreement will come from the trilateral meeting, according to a senior U.S. official, who described the session as an “entry point” and “the first conversation,” pointing to the reduction of nuclear arsenals as a key topic.

“We do think it’s time for China to sort of step up, you know, to the adults’ table, if you will, and have adult conversations about adult things,” the senior U.S. official said about the issue of nuclear weapons.

Beijing’s arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the U.S. and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With U.S. and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.

The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernized” deal that includes China.
The three-way summit with Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin comes at a complicated moment in relations for the three countries.

Trump intends to discuss the Iran war with the two leaders, but not the war in Ukraine, according to a senior U.S. official, who noted that discussions about the war in Ukraine are a separate “track” that China is not part of so it would not be “appropriate.”

Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the U.S. war with Iran and other tensions between the world’s foremost economic powers.

Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin, even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly 5-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.
There is no bilateral with Putin scheduled, but the two leaders will appear at events and the trilateral meeting together, according to a senior U.S. official.
There are no plans for Trump to engage with North Korea during the trip, according to a senior U.S. official.

Separately, Elon Musk will be the only business leader who is part of the president’s delegation, according to a senior U.S. official, who noted that other U.S. business leaders will attend the summit in their own capacity but there is no official U.S. business delegation.
Musk will not be part of any official meetings, according to a senior U.S. official.

Two senior U.S. officials said that they don’t think Trump will raise the espionage investigation focused on Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence agent who allegedly had a romantic relationship with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, with China.

“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip. In all of our discussions and negotiations with the Chinese, we do not negotiate American export controls,” a senior U.S. official said. “These are national security matters that we develop in the administration and interagency process, and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there.”
Beijing was least certain about the value of the summit
By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China’s growing clout and prestige.
For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.
For Subscribers

“I think the key for Putin was that this was very much about signaling a desire to talk to the president and talk to Chairman Xi in a way that suggests that they’re making decisions on Ukraine, which obviously the Ukrainians and the Europeans don’t like,” said Edgard Kagan, a former U.S. ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
For Subscribers

The trilateral could very well overshadow the APEC summit. The summit, which is bringing 21 economies to Shenzhen, marks a big moment for China to show off its fast-growing, ultramodern coastal metropolis that transformed from a small fishing village into a global technology and economic hub in just a few decades.

More substantively, such a gathering could also muddy China’s argument that a Cold War mentality in the West was a contributing factor that led to Russia’s war on Ukraine and its pointed criticism that the U.S. has undermined international institutions and treaties with how it has executed its war against Iran.

The trilateral meeting could undercut China’s push to portray itself as a defender of free trade at APEC, said Hoo Tiang Boon, a professor of Chinese foreign policy at Nanyang Technological University.
“You sort of run counter to Chinese support of multilateralism,” he said.
The leaders have met in pairs plenty of times over the years
Putin and Xi are no strangers. They’ve fostered a close personal relationship, meeting more than 40 times since Xi became president in 2013 and addressing each other as “dear friend.”

Trump and Putin have met face-to-face on seven different occasions, most recently in Alaska in August 2025. Xi and Trump have held face-to-face talks on eight occasions, including a September state visit to Washington by Xi.
Beijing is the No. 1 trading partner for Moscow, a relationship that has strengthened since Putin sent troops into Ukraine in 2022.

As the EU and the West sought to economically isolate Russia, China increased its purchases of Russia’s energy resources and became Moscow’s principal supplier of key technologies, including high-tech components for Russian weapons industries. Beijing has ignored Western demands to cut those supplies.

In the lead-up to Russia’s war on Ukraine, Xi and Putin declared their countries had a “no-limits friendship.” China officially has said it is neutral on the conflict, while charging that Kyiv’s Western allies played a part in provoking Russia’s military action in Ukraine.
Moscow, in turn, has repeatedly declared its support for Beijing’s policy on issues related to Taiwan.

Trump recently struck a diesel deal with Russia, waiving sanctions against Moscow and allowing for the sale of millions of tons of the fuel. The U.S. leader has blamed surging energy prices on Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries. Analysts, however, say the rise in global crude prices is due mostly to the Iran war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concern that the trilateral meeting could serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv’s back.

Planning for the summit has drawn comparisons to the Yalta Conference, the 1945 gathering at which the leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union agreed to divide Germany and Berlin into four military occupation zones and finalized plans for establishing the United Nations.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has dismissed the Yalta comparisons, noting that any potential agreements reached in Shenzhen can’t be enforced on others.

“It’s clear that a meeting between the leaders of countries such as Russia, China and the United States is extremely significant,” Peskov said. “However, let’s not forget that the vision for a global order is that no one tries to impose any particular view of global order, and it should be based entirely on mutual benefit and mutual respect.”

title: Newly elected Senate Democrats in the spotlight: From the Politics Desk
summary: In today’s edition, Kristen Welker dives into the first big decision facing the class of incoming Democratic senators.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

In today’s edition, Kristen Welker dives into the first big decision facing the class of incoming Democratic senators. Plus, Natasha Korecki explains why the midterm results could make Democrats’ 2028 presidential primary even more unwieldy.
— Adam Wollner
Newly elected Democrats in the spotlight as Senate leadership fight kicks off
The first battle in the fight for the future of the Democratic Party will come next month, when Senate Democrats choose who their leader will be when they are in the majority next year.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., announced last night that he is challenging Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., who has led the Democratic caucus in the chamber for a decade. And all eyes will be on the 13 newly elected Democrats joining the Senate.

Many of the incoming freshman Democrats have been calling for change, but Schumer’s role in recruiting some of them and helping them win their races also looms large. Schumer’s supporters have likened ousting him to firing a baseball manager who just won the World Series.

Two newly elected Democrats — Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota — have already said that they will support Van Hollen for majority leader. Four others — Maine’s Troy Jackson, South Carolina’s Annie Andrews, Illinois’ Juliana Stratton and Kansas’ Adam Hamilton — have publicly said they would oppose Schumer.

“What I’d be looking for is a leader who can lead from the center, somebody who can bring Republicans and Democrats together, somebody who can bring the various factions in Democratic Party together, somebody with fresh ideas,” Hamilton told me on “Meet the Press” on Sunday. “So again, no disrespect for Chuck Schumer. Just, it feels like there’s time for — it is a time for fresh and new ideas and somebody who can unite us instead of dividing us.

Just one incoming Democratic senator has said he will back Schumer: Ohio’s Sherrod Brown, who served three terms in the chamber before losing in 2024. Brown told NBC affiliate WCMH of Columbus that he was supporting Schumer “because I think he knows how to govern.”
“He’s controversial, people think he hasn’t fought hard enough. But that’s up to people like me to make sure he does,” said Brown, whom Schumer encouraged to run.

Another candidate Schumer heavily recruited, former Gov. Roy Cooper of North Carolina, told CNN earlier this year that he has “made no commitments” about whom he would support as leader. Schumer also recruited former Rep. Mary Peltola, who is locked in a close race in Alaska that is too early to call, and it is not clear how she would vote if she wins.
The other newly elected Democrats have been noncommittal.

Iowa’s Josh Turek told me late last year that “the party needs change” and he would press candidates for leader on what they could do for his state. Texas’ James Talarico told CBS News after winning his race that he wants to meet with every leadership candidate. And New Hampshire’s Chris Pappas told CNN earlier this year that “it’s time for new voices” and he would wait to see who is running.
For Subscribers

The latest Democrat to flip a Senate seat — Mississippi’s Scott Colom — has expressed concerns about Schumer and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, the likely next speaker of the House, both hailing from the same New York City borough. But he told MS NOW this morning that he is “not a no” on Schumer and he wants the next leader to prioritize the Deep South and “actually fight for rural America.”
For Subscribers

Ultimately, Schumer will need to secure majority support from the Senate Democratic caucus. After Van Hollen joined the race, Schumer expressed confidence, saying on X, “I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader.”

Colom will join me to discuss all of this and more on “Meet the Press” this Sunday. Former Vice President Mike Pence, who recently suggested he could make another run for the White House, will also join for an exclusive interview.
Blue wave ignites a wild, wide-open 2028 race

DENVER — Last week’s Democratic midterm sweep reached so far and so wide that it is already recasting conventional thinking about who can forge a winning path to the White House in 2028 — blowing the doors off of what was already expected to be a wide-open presidential race.

There was something for everyone in Democratic politics. Moderates won, but so did progressives. Women scored victories in deep-red, statewide races. Candidates who didn’t have the most money won. Democrats won in the South and in rural states and districts. They scored big gains among young men and noncollege white voters. They also showed they could win back Hispanic voters.

It has all scrambled the thinking for an upcoming 2028 presidential primary, potentially opening more paths to winning the Electoral College than Democrats have had or considered in years. That’s likely to lure even more White House hopefuls to join what is expected to be a crowded field.

“It’s going to be the craziest, most wide-open primary,” said Brian Stryker, a longtime Democratic pollster. “I wouldn’t bet on anyone against the field. I wouldn’t say anyone has more than a 50% chance. I don’t know if anyone has more than a 20% chance.”

title: Ground stop lifted hours after stranding thousands of flights across the U.S.
summary: U.S. air traffic was brought to a standstill Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop for departing flights that lasted more than four hours.
story: U.S. air traffic was brought to a standstill Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop for departing flights that lasted more than four hours.
The FAA lifted the ground stop at 8:15 p.m. ET, after more than 7,000 flights were canceled and airports across the country became packed with stranded, irritated passengers.

The sudden and stunning alert was issued at 3:54 p.m. ET, “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the FAA said. It offered no other information beyond stating that “all departing traffic should remain ground stopped until further notice.”

Hours later, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, in a White House news conference Friday evening, blamed the outage on an outdated air traffic control system in which the routers “got overloaded with data.”
By Friday evening, Delta Air Lines, United, American said they were resuming flights.
What caused the ground stop
Duffy explained that once the routers became overloaded, it led to “instability for our radar and our communications in our centers, in our TRACONS throughout the country.”
TRACON stands for Terminal Radar Approach Control and is an air traffic control center.
“The TRACONS and the centers, we started to have inconsistency in the data from the radars and our communication with airplanes,” Duffy said.
That instability was detected at 3:36 p.m., he said.
Duffy said the FAA did not lose all telecom or radar capabilities but because of the instability, the ground stop was issued as a cautionary measure.

It’ll take time for the airspace to recover from the ground stop as crews and planes are out of place and staffers may have reached on-duty shift limitations. However, Duffy said he anticipates American airspace will catch up before Thanksgiving travel rush.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no sign of a cyberattack and the public was never in danger.

“FAA was able to handle it. We did it out of an abundance of caution,” he said in a news conference from the White House Friday night. Earlier on Friday, he described the issue as a telecommunications outage.

At the time of the ground stop, there were over 3,500 airplanes in the air, Duffy said. When the FAA issued the alert, 4,042 flights headed for U.S. destinations were airborne, according to Flightradar24, a Swedish service that displays real-time aircraft flight tracking information.

Friday’s ground stop is perhaps the most severe consequence of what Duffy described as a decades-old air traffic control system using analog equipment, which has led to several issues and outages over the past few years.
In May 2025, radar screens at Newark Liberty International Airport’s went black during a 90-second outage.

Duffy said the legacy equipment will continue to fail and pushed Congress to approve $50 billion to overhaul the  system. Congress last year approved $12.5 billion over five years to upgrade air traffic control, Reuters reported.
Mullin said earlier Friday that President Donald Trump was briefed on the ground stop.
Mullin said though authorities cannot rule out a cyberattack, there was no evidence to suggest that. “There’s nothing completely certain right now. It doesn’t appear that way,” he said.

Meanwhile, Air Space Intelligence, the AI tech startup that is a vendor for the FAA on its new SMART system for air traffic control, insisted its software was not responsible for the nationwide ground stop.
“The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC,” the company said in a statement posted to X.
Duffy said the SMART system is “completely disconnected” from the equipment that suffered issues Friday.
Packed airports

Several hours after the ground stop was announced, a top aviation expert estimated that anywhere from 300,000 to 400,000 passengers were stranded — and it was anybody’s guess when they would get to their destinations.

“Daily, we have about 25,000 flights in U.S. domestic markets,” Vikrant Vaze, a Dartmouth professor who specializes in commercial aviation logistics, wrote in an email to NBC News. “I would say we should have around 3,000 to 4,000 flights held up at this time over the past 2 plus hours.”

But by 6 p.m., Reagan Washington National Airport in Arlington, Virginia, was at capacity, and Chicago O’Hare International Airport was nearing capacity, meaning there was no place for the planes to park, a source with knowledge told NBC News.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
With planes stranded on runways, the likelihood increased that some of these planes would have to be diverted to other airports, the source said.
Aviation safety expert Jeff Guzzetti called the outage “extraordinary.”

Guzzetti emphasized that pilots are trained to operate through communications outages and that there are redundancies in place for such instances. Pilots “could get information relayed through other means” to ensure planes are spaced properly for landing.
There are different layers of communications — high-altitude, midlevel and the towers on the ground. The high-altitude control centers are the ones affected by the outage.

At Newark Liberty International Airport, personnel in the control tower said the situation is “a whole mess right now,” according to LiveATC. “We’re running out of space” and “there’s significant gate issues” were comments also heard on the live audio feed.
“I’m as much in the dark as everyone else. I’m not getting any information from anybody,” one controller at Newark said, according to the feed.

Shortly before the FAA issued its alert, both major airports in Chicago — O’Hare and Midway International Airport — were listed on a ground stop alert due to an “equipment outage,” NBC Chicago reported.
Deveren Werne was on an American Airlines jet that was about to take off from Indianapolis to Chicago when suddenly the pilots announced that all flights were grounded.

“At first, the pilot announced that there was some kind of radio issue,” Werne, 55, of Greenville, South Carolina, told NBC News in a telephone interview. “Then a little while later, the pilot said something like, ‘There is something going on that’s more serious than that.’”

Werne, a consultant who helps manufacturers and other industries adapt AI technology, said he is a frequent flyer and this was a first for him. He said there was “a mixture of emotions” from his fellow passengers on hearing the announcement.

“Then I started hearing from other friends who were on planes, including one in Chicago who was stuck on a runway,” Werne said. “Right now, our plane is heading back to the terminal, so at least we’re going to be able to deplane.”
Medical flights, such as for organ transplants, were not stopped during the ground stop, Duffy said.
Nationwide ground stops are extremely rare
Ground stops across the nation are a rarity in U.S. history.

After the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, the FAA ordered an unprecedented nationwide ground stop. All civilian air traffic across U.S. airspace was halted and airborne planes were ordered to land at the nearest available airports.
In January 2023, the FAA grounded all flights for a few hours, blaming a failure in the Notice to Air Missions system, which alerts pilots to a host of potential dangers.

Officials at the time blamed contract personnel for the outage, saying they accidentally deleted files while working to correct the synchronization between databases. The error prompted a computer outage that lasted approximately an hour and a half, Department of Transportation officials said at the time.

title: Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy Break Down  ‘The Good Daughter’ Ending, From Emotional Moments to Plot Twists
summary: Warning: Spoilers ahead for “The Good Daughter.” The new Peacock series takes a turn when it comes to discovering who was behind the sisters’ trauma, shooting and more.
story: Warning: Spoilers ahead for “The Good Daughter.”
Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy bring to life author Karin Slaughter’s best-selling psychological thriller “The Good Daughter” in the new Peacock series, out Nov. 12.

The actors portray trauma-bonded yet resilient, estranged sisters Charlotte “Charlie” (Fahy) and Samantha “Sam” (Byrne) Quinn, who reunite after one of them unintentially becomes involved in a murder case involving a young student.

Over the course of the six-episode miniseries, viewers discover how an attack on their family when the sisters were teens ended with the death of mother, Gamma (Olivia Williams), life-altering injuries for Sam, Charlie being sexually assaulted and their defense attorney father Rusty (Brendon Gleeson) forever changed.

Flash forward over two decades later, and the sisters, both lawyers, are reunited after Sam returns to town to help her father with a case. After a one-night stand with a man named Mason “Huck” (Jake McDorman), Charlie visits him at the school he works at and witnesses a shooting.

An 18-year-old named Kelly (Shayna Benardo) is accused of shooting Principal Douglas Pinkman and another student. But something doesn’t add up. As the family gets involved in the case, the sisters become haunted by their past attackers and townspeople, who blame them for what they believe are injustices.
The final episode, titled “What Really Happened,” does just that, revealing who actually shot Pinkman. It also shares more insight into who was involved in the sisters’ attack.

“It’s very rare for anyone to figure out the real truth of this story, and that’s by design. And I’ve been plotting thrillers for a long time,” author and showrunner Slaughter tells TODAY.com. “I think it was one of my strengths to make you think one thing, and then suddenly it’s another. I love playing with expectations that way. Anybody who wants a good thriller will be wholly satisfied.”

“But you know,” she adds, “one of the things about writing a thriller about families is there’s also emotional suspense, and that underlying tension of what’s going on between Sam and Charlie, and where we’re going to leave them propels you through the show as much as the whodunit.”
Here’s what happens at the end of “The Good Daughter.”

Mason was one of the men who was present when their mom was shot and they were attacked. Ben (Michael Dorman), Charlie’s estranged husband and Pikeville’s assistant district attorney, finds Mason’s written confession inside Rusty’s home.
The sisters previously knew that Zach Culpepper Jr. was behind the attack, but because the other man called his accomplice “brother,” they assumed it was his sibling Daniel Culpepper. It wasn’t.

Mason had given Zach Culpepper Jr. $5,000 to kill Rusty after he successfully represented a man in court who sexually assaulted Mason’s sister. Rusty got the man a lighter sentence, and Mason’s sister killed herself, so he wanted revenge.

During the attack, Mason was able to talk Zach out of killing the sisters and pushed him off Charlie when she was being sexually assaulted, but the damage was done. He told the sisters he tried to confess, but his parents wouldn’t let him.

After Rusty dies, his daughters are tasked with executing his final wishes. While going through his office, they discover dozens of letters that read “You Owe Me,” and $2,000 checks made out to Zach Culpepper Jr.

After Mason’s confession, they realize that Zach Jr. was being paid every month to keep the truth quiet about Mason’s involvement in the Quinn family attack. Mason insisted it was his parents who made the deal and he found out 10 years ago.

Mason first confessed to Rusty after he found out about the hush payments when his mother was dying. Rusty did not want his daughters to relive their trauma and become entrenched in a new trail, so he had Mason hand over the money that was for Zach Jr and write down his confession, which Ben later found.
Asked if Rusty forgave him, Mason said no.
Why did Rusty want to control the money? Mason said it was so that one day Charlie and Sam could decide if they wanted to keep paying Zach Jr. or show Mason’s confession to the cops.
They call the cops on Mason, but for a different reason. Mason had stolen the gun Kelly used to shoot Principal Pinkman. If he got convicted for taking the weapon, he would get 10 years in prison.

The sisters and Ben discuss their options, breaking down how even if Zach Jr. stops getting paid and Zach Sr. confesses Mason’s involvement, a long legal battle would ensue. Their discussion brings them back to Kelly’s case and if she was responsible for Principal Pinkman’s death.
Kelly brought a gun to school and did plan to shoot Principal Doug, but as Charlie and Sam discover, it wasn’t her idea.
During Kelly’s court cases, it is revealed that she is pregnant. But who is the father? It’s actually Principal Pinkman.
The principal’s wife, Judith (Paula Malcomson), was the one who orchestrated the shooting. Charlie goes over to Judith’s home and Judith confesses.

Judith witnessed her husband sexually assaulting Kelly and learned that the teen was pregnant. Her husband told her that they would take care of the baby, which infuriated her. Judith then kept scaring Kelly about her and her baby’s future, until she convinced her to kill her husband.

The day of the shooting, Judith put her fingers over Kelly’s hand and pulled the trigger. She struggled to take the gun from Kelly, and they accidentally shot another other student. Judith said she planned on also shooting Kelly to avoid the teen confessing, but she didn’t have enough bullets. Her plan to be seen as the mourning widow and get her husband’s insurance money was unsuccessful.
As Judith confesses, Charlie records their conversation, while Sam and Ben listen from outside. Judith loads her gun and demands that Charlie leave her home. Judith then kills herself.
With Judith’s confession, Kelly gets five years of prison time since she was still involved in the murders.
The series ends with Charlie and Sam back at Rusty’s, going through his belongings. Ben and Charlie have decided they are moving to Atlanta.

Meanwhile, the sisters are looking for a photo of their mom that their dad had wanted them to find. They find the photo in the back of another picture frame. On the back it has a message for them, “Last word.”
Byrne tells TODAY.com she wouldn’t want to tell the audience what to feel or think, but at the end, part of her hopes the sisters continue to work on their relationship.
“The reconciliation is such a joyful thing,” she says, adding that she hopes they continue to be “in one another’s lives.”
Fahy agrees, also telling TODAY.com, “I really imagine that when we leave them, they are in each other’s lives in a big and beautiful way moving forward.”

title: Avril Lavigne Announces Birth of First Child, a Baby Girl — See the Pics
summary: Avril Lavigne just announced the cutest damn thing.
story: Avril Lavigne just announced the cutest damn thing.
The punk rocker shared on Instagram Nov. 13 that she just welcomed her first child. And the “Sk8er Boi” singer made the announcement in a way that would make any millennial emo kid proud.
“Our Mini F------ Princess has arrived 🎀👑🍼🩷,” Lavigne wrote in the post.
The 42-year-old mom did not reveal the identity of the child’s father.

In the Instagram post, Lavigne shared a series of photos, including one that featured what appeared to be the rocker’s hand and that of her mystery partner, holding their newborn’s tiny fingers. Another snap showed Lavigne, clutching her baby girl who’s decked out in a leopard print onesie.
The final photo in the slideshow features three pairs of Vans sneakers on a skateboard, symbolizing the new family of three. The snap also appears to be a sweet nod to her 2002 hit “Sk8er Boi.”

Lavigne, who’s best known for her 2002 debut album “Let Go,” has been relatively private about her personal life. However, she’s had several high-profile relationships including a marriage to Sum 41’s Deryck Whibley from 2006 to 2010 and another to Nickelback’s Chad Kroeger from 2013 to 2015.
She was also briefly engaged to musician Mod Sun in 2022.

title: NFL Quarterback Sam Hartman Is Named the Next ‘Bachelor.’ The 1 Quality He Wants in a Match
summary: Bachelor Nation can add a new football player to its roster.
story: Bachelor Nation can add a new football player to its roster.
Sam Hartman, a quarterback for The Washington Commanders, was just revealed as the new star of “The Bachelor.”

The professional athlete joins a growing list of NFL players who have taken their quest for love to the ABC dating series over the years. Prior football players who have been the show’s lead include Jessie Palmer, who now hosts “The Bachelor,” and Colton Underwood.
The official Instagram page for “The Bachelor” shared a photo of Hartman Nov. 13, captioning the post, “the next Bachelor 🌹.”
Hartman also appeared on “Good Morning America” to discuss his upcoming season of the show, which will premiere on March 21 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC.

The 27-year-old admitted that he first said, “No way!” when asked to appear on “The Bachelor” since he was worried about “the connotation” of finding love on reality TV. But Palmer, a former football pro turned “Bachelor,” helped change his mind.
“He kind of gave me the inside and gave me kind of what it is, what it’s not,” he said.
The Charlotte, N.C. native said he’s seeking one key characteristic in his future partner: competitiveness.

“(I’m looking for) competitiveness in somebody that I want to be able to chase. Not chase in a way that you haven’t texted me back in a week, but chase in a way that they have a drive for something and motivate me every day to wake up and chase them,” he said.

Hartman, who played college football for Wake Forest University and the University of Notre Dame, said he’s also looking for a woman with “compassion,” possibly someone who works in a field where they provide “some type of caregiving.”
“My whole family is in the medicine field,” he said.
Hartman spoke about his upcoming adventure on “The Bachelor”  the morning after his team beat the New York Giants in a Nov. 12 match.
The NFL player is used to being calm under pressure while playing in packed stadiums, but he admitted that he’s “very nervous” to start his journey on “The Bachelor.”
“I have a tough time holding a conversation with one girl. Thirty is gonna be pretty tough,” he said.
Hartman’s teammates have been giving him some words of wisdom as he prepares to find love. But he joked that he’s “probably not gonna listen” to their advice.
The quarterback doesn’t expect to find somebody who’s as skilled at football as he is, but said the ladies vying for his attention will certainly have to show off their football skills.
“They’ve gotta be ready to bring their competitive spirit,” he said.

title: How ‘I Play Rocky’ Actor Anthony Ippolito Nailed the Iconic Sylvester Stallone Voice
summary: At first listen, Anthony Ippolito’s voice in biographical Sylvester Stallone film “I Play Rocky” is startling, not because of its tenor or pitch — but because of its striking familiarity.
story: At first listen, Anthony Ippolito’s voice in biographical Sylvester Stallone film “I Play Rocky” is startling, not because of its tenor or pitch — but because of its striking familiarity.

That husky, unmistakable New York accent is what so many “Rocky” fans have grown up hearing against the film’s rough, Philadelphia backdrop and that symphonic Bill Conti soundtrack. And yet, the speaker isn’t Stallone at all.

Ippolito, who plays Sly in the film, spoke to TODAY.com ahead of the film’s nationwide release Nov. 20. He said that he was well aware that the character was profoundly meaningful to people across different generations, so he “didn’t take it lightly.”
And that meant doing some intense research, unearthing as much footage as he could from Stallone’s early years when Sly was still trying to make it in acting.
“It was actually pretty difficult in some ways because he wasn’t a huge movie star at that point,” Ippolito said.
He added that he “just really wanted to find everything I could on him and put my best foot forward.”

Based on Stallone’s own life, the film tells the story of a young Sly, who’s desperate to get his film career going, but sees little promise in actually nabbing a substantial role. With few prospects and a baby on the way, the doggedly ambitious Stallone decides that the only sure-fire path to success is by writing a blockbuster film — and casting himself as the lead. The story, one that peels back the curtain on how the now-timeless “Rocky” was truly made, ultimately explores the power of belief in oneself and the indomitable human spirit.

But bringing to the screen an authentic portrayal of Stallone — a man whose reputation as a heroic action star has risen to near-legendary levels — was no simple task. And Ippolito says he was up for the challenge.

“It was a lot to take in and a little daunting at the beginning, especially. But I was also excited. I think that this part of his story is one that some people knew, but not enough,” Ippolito tells TODAY.com. “So I was really happy to have any hand in helping you know people understand this part of it because it’s incredible.

Ippolito, who did not have a voice coach for the gig, explains that he perfected the voice by watching any clips he could find of old Stallone interviews and the action star’s early supporting roles. He also said that much of his prepwork involved understanding Stallone’s partial facial paralysis and how it impacted his speech. Stallone was delivered by a physician who used forceps to pull him out, Sly has said on many occasions. The delivery left him with a severed facial nerve on his left side.

“That facial paralysis caused by the birth accident with forceps created this change in his voice and also a bit of a slur,” Ippolito said. “He had to grow up dealing with that and dealing with the judgment that came with that over the course of his youth.”

Luckily, Ippolito was also able to get some tips from Sly himself. It’s something, Ippolito says, that was particularly useful as details about the nascent stages of his career aren’t so widely available or publicized.

“This really isn’t about that period of time after Rocky where he became a star. It was more so about the period of struggle and loneliness and isolation that he was in,” Ippolito explains. “Getting to speak to him about that period of time was really really helpful, getting to hear firsthand the toll that that takes on you growing up and the types of adversity that he was facing.”
Ippolito says that he felt “privileged” to learn from the man himself.

“It’s kind of a vulnerable thing, right? This is a very pivotal time in his life, and it’s a not very polished period of time,” he says. “I just really appreciated him 50 years after the fact being able to share it with me.”

Stallone, of course, has seen the film and he’s been open about how impressed he’s been with Ippolito’s portrayal. Even in the project’s earliest stages, Stallone was already moved by Ippolito’s commitment to the character.
“The text that Sly sent us after we watched Anthony’s tape, I’ll never forget,” producer Toby Emmerich told NBC News. “He said, ‘This is not an impersonation. This is a performance.’”
Ippolito’s reaction is one of humility.
“He was very, very kind,” Ippolito says.

title: See a First Look at Mel and Jack With Their Baby as ‘Virgin River’ Is Officially Renewed for Season 9
summary: “Virgin River” has officially been renewed for a landmark Season 9 on Netflix. See a photo of what’s ahead for Mel and Jack as they welcome a baby to their family.
story: “Virgin River” has officially been renewed for a landmark Season 9 on Netflix, becoming the longest-running original scripted drama series on the platform, and TODAY.com has an exclusive first look at what’s ahead.

The Season 9 renewal comes ahead of the release of Season 8, which is set to premiere in 2027. Last season ended on a major cliffhanger as Mel and Jack finally became parents but had to rush their newborn son into emergency surgery.

TODAY.com can exclusively share a new photo from Episode 1 of Season 8 of the characters, played by Alexandra Breckenridge and Martin Henderson, sharing a sweet moment with their baby boy. In the photo, an emotional Jack holds his son as Mel stares lovingly into her husband’s eyes and rests a hand on the baby’s head.
It’s a well-deserved moment of peace for the couple, whose challenging journey to parenthood has been a major focal point of the show.

In Season 7, they agreed to adopt the unborn child of a young woman named Marley (Rachel Drance) then found their future hanging in the balance as Marley’s ex-boyfriend (and the father of her child) came to town. Marley decided to go through with the adoption, then learned her baby had a congenital heart defect and would need emergency surgery after birth.
An exact premiere date for Season 8 hasn’t been announced yet, but the season will premiere next year.

In addition to releasing a sneak peek at Season 8, Netflix gave fans a double dose of glee Nov. 13 as the streaming service announced Season 9’s renewal, which will have 10 episodes. “Virgin River” is based on Robyn Carr’s book series of the same name, which has more than 20 installments.

“I’m incredibly proud of our show and couldn’t be more thrilled to have the opportunity to continue into Season 9!” Breckenridge said in a statement. “Everyone on our production works so hard to make the world of ‘Virgin River’ come alive. It’s truly been a gift to be here,” she said.
Henderson echoed his co-star’s sentiments.
“It’s staggering to think we are still making ‘Virgin River’ after all these years and I’m delighted to get to play the role of Jack for the ninth straight season!” he said in a statement.

The actor thanked the show’s fans, saying the cast and crew “wouldn’t be here without them all,” and he said they’re eager to “keep making it to the best of our ability” as long as fans want to watch the show.

title: The Gift Robert Irwin Gave Witney Carson’s Sons That They’re Already Sharing With Baby No. 3
summary: Witney Carson says everyone in her family is preparing for the arrival of her third baby in their own exciting way, especially her sons Kevin Leo and Jet Carson.
story: Witney Carson says everyone in her family is preparing for the arrival of her third baby in their own exciting way, especially her sons Kevin Leo and Jet Carson.
The “Dancing With the Stars” pro announced in August that she was pregnant and by September revealed she was having another boy.

“Every day, I’m like, ‘Oh my gosh, I’m actually going to have three babies.’ So some days I’m overwhelmed, and some days I’m feeling very excited,” she tells TODAY.com. “And I think the boys are very excited too.”
Her sons are so thrilled to have a baby brother that they’re already sharing their toys with baby on the way, including a gift from Robert Irwin.

“Robert Irwin gifted them two huge crocodiles, and they put them in baby brother’s crib because they really want baby brother to sleep with these two huge crocodiles,” Carson says. “So they’re doing little things like that that are very sweet and thoughtful.”
Carson and Irwin competed on and won Season 34 of “DWTS”together, cultivating a great friendship with each other’s families in the process.
She loves that her sons are “thinking about” their sibling, “which is so cute.” However, she notes, “The crocodile, he won’t be sleeping with those. But it was a good thought.”

Just like her sons have already done a sweet gesture for their brother, Carson is also giving back and partnering with Pampers to give 50 families the chance to win $1,500 to help fulfill their registries.
The dancer says she hopes to relieve any stress when it comes to expenses, which “can really add up.”
“At a time where it’s supposed to be very exciting, we want to take that load off parents and allow them to just enjoy.”

She also understands how wonderful it is to have the support of friends and family during a pregnancy. But one thing she was so happy about was feeling the love from other parents while competing on Season 35 with Guillermo Rodriguez.

“I love being a mom and I love to dance. And so the fact that I could do both was such a huge blessing. And I really did prove to myself that I could do it, and I think in turn it kind of showed other women that as well,” Carson, who is due in February, says. “Which wasn’t my  mission or anything, but it really just kind of turned into that.”
She adds that the support she felt from parents, from moms, “from people who really were cheering me on and rooting for me felt so empowering.”
“And that really allowed me to keep going day by day, to keep doing better, to keep showing up,” she says.

title: Michael B. Jordan Sends Special Message to TODAY to Reveal Trailer for ‘The Thomas Crown Affair’
summary: The official trailer for Michael B. Jordan’s “The Thomas Crown Affair” is finally here, TODAY can exclusively reveal, along with a special message from the star himself.
story: The official trailer for Michael B. Jordan’s “The Thomas Crown Affair” is finally here, TODAY can exclusively reveal, along with a special message from the star himself.
“To be able to reimagine and give my version of this story and this character means the world to me and my incredible cast,” he said in a video message for TODAY.
The romantic heist drama was also written, directed and produced by Jordan.
“The Thomas Crown Affair” is set to hit theaters on March 5, 2027. Jordan, who plays protagonist Thomas Crown, stars opposite Adria Arjona.

This is the third take on the Thomas Crown story. The first film, which debuted in 1968, starred Steve McQueen and Faye Dunaway. In 1999, Pierce Brosnan and Rene Russo brought the heist film’s central romance to life.
Amazon MGM Studios describes the new film as a “visually breathtaking, sensual, and unexpectedly moving heist thriller, where the most dangerous man in the room is the one nobody’s watching.”
To celebrate the premiere of the trailer, Jordan filmed an exclusive video for TODAY and explained just how meaningful it was to work on the film.

“I’ve been in love with this IP and this story and this character for such a long time,” he said. “The first time I got a chance to see Pierce Brosnan and Rene Russo was in high school. I went back and saw what an amazing job Steve McQueen and Faye Dunaway did with the original Thomas Crown in ‘68.”
Now Jordan is giving the story his own twist.
“To be able to reimagine and give my version of this story and this character means the world to me and my incredible cast,” he said.
The trailer previews Jordan and Arjona’s romantic cat-and-mouse dynamic. Per Variety, she plays a former FBI agent who is hunting down Crown after he orchestrates a heist.
“Tell me Mr. Crown, do you like taking risks?” she says.
“Only if it’s worth it,” he replies.

Viewers learn that a thief (seemingly Crown) has stolen five pieces of artwork from across the globe over the last decade. But all Crown really wants to do is return stolen and sold artifacts to their creators.
Action, intrigue and seduction ensue.
“Something tells me that once you set your eyes on something, you won’t stop until you get it,” Jordan’s character tells Arjona’s. You think you’ll get me?”
Jordan previously told Variety he wanted to make a “re-imagination” of the Thomas Crown story, rather than a reboot.
“The first two films were about rich white guys stealing for fun. That doesn’t land today,” he said. “Ours is more personal. The stakes are higher. Still got the fashion, romance.”

title: One Direction Makes Its US TV Debut on TODAY in 2012
summary: One Direction made its American televison debut on TODAY on March 12, 2012.
story: As TODAY marks its 75th anniversary, the TODAY Archive is revisiting legendary interviews, stories that moved us and other iconic moments from our 75 years on the air. These are the segments that shaped TODAY and created a lasting legacy. Today, we look back at One Direction making its American television debut on March 12, 2012.
One Direction would begin its stateside conquest on March 12, 2012, when the group made its American television debut on TODAY.

The quintet, made up of Niall Horan, Liam Payne, Harry Styles, Louis Tomlinson and Zayn Malik, performed for an adoring and raucous crowd. The group was ushered into the Plaza atop a double decker bus before making its way to the stage. On a brisk day when the temperature was 55 degrees, the fellas quickly made things sizzle as they greeted those in attendance.
“New York City, make some noise!” Styles urged the fans, who followed with wild cheering.
What Did One Direction Sing?
The guys then launched into one of their earliest trademark hits, “What Makes You Beautiful,” as the crowd below sang along with them. Hoda Kotb even captured the moment on her phone.
By the time the 1D finished, the crowd was in a total frenzy, having cheered, sung along and snapped photos of the performance. You could say it was an in-Zayn reaction.
When Did One Direction Return to TODAY?
One Direction would return in 2013 to perform again, with an estimated 18,000 people on hand.
“It seems to me this is the biggest crowd we’ve ever had,” Al Roker said at the time.
What Did One Direction Think About Its Success?
One Direction split in 2015 after Malik’s surprising decision to leave and was rocked when Payne died in 2024 after he fell from a third floor hotel balcony in Argentina
Still, the band was massive in its day and took off quickly with the success of “What Makes You Beautiful.”
“It snowballed very fast,” Horan told Willie Geist in 2023. “And the rest is history, I suppose.”
Horan was also able to put that time into perspective.
“It nearly feels like it’s a separate life now,” he said.

title: Brandon Sklenar Opens Up About Experiencing Body Dysmorphia Since He Was 12
summary: Actor Brandon Sklenar opens up about struggling with body dysmorphia from a young age and how the experience inspired his performance in the upcoming sports drama “Iron Jane.”
story: Actor Brandon Sklenar is opening up about struggling with body dysmorphia from a young age and how the experience inspired his performance in the upcoming sports drama “Iron Jane.”

The “1923” star, 36, explained his personal connection to his next project, which also stars Eiza González, in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter. “Iron Jane” tells the story of a woman (González) who undergoes an intense transformation to become a competitive bodybuilder following a difficult childhood. Sklenar plays the former champion who guides her.
Sklenar told the magazine he was intrigued by the film after previously working in an underground bodybuilding gym.

“I personally was drawn to it because I grew up in northern New Jersey working in an underground bodybuilding gym. When I was 15, I was cleaning the floors, and by 18, I was a trainer, training everybody and running the whole gym,” he shared. “There was an MMA gym upstairs, and I would just train MMA all day and then train other people. I started doing martial arts when I was really little, like six.”
Since he used to work and train in that world, he saw firsthand the posing, diets and steroids that are involved.

Sklenar noted, “There is an element of ‘Iron Jane’ that really goes into body image and body dysmorphia, which is something that I just really feel needs to be talked about more, especially in this age of social media and fitness influencers.”

“This is something I’ve struggled with, so we really wanted to translate that, and (director Lissette Feliciano) was really open to working with me on getting across (my character) Josh’s dysmorphia and what he goes through,” he added.
“The Housemaid” star shared more details about his past struggles, revealing that they began when he was a child.

“I was a little kid — short, chunky. I swam in a T-shirt and got made fun of. Then I had a growth spurt and became really lanky, and I got made fun of for that,” he recalled. “So I started training a lot and got obsessed with working out, like, ‘I’ll show them.’”
The desire to prove them wrong turned into “a kind of obsession,” he said.
“It becomes a very weird thing, where you see yourself completely differently than pretty much anybody else does, and usually in not a good way,” he explained.
Sklenar said he is still tackling his body image issues.

“Therapy helps for sure. If you look at me now as a 36-year-old man, you’d never guess it, but I still very much feel like that 12-year-old chunky kid — that sense of nothing is ever good enough,” he revealed. “You have to find a way to check your self-talk, because that’s really where it begins and ends — but it’s easier said than done.”
He said that working on “Iron Jane” allowed him to confront some of his insecurities. He shared details of one scene that includes a full-body shot as he poses.

“I’ve been pretty much naked in a film before, but it’s a whole different thing to literally be posing and have the camera panning up and down your body, detailing everything. When I was shooting that scene, I was so uncomfortable. Dealing with my issues, it was very challenging to work through that,” he pointed out.
But, Sklenar said he reminded himself that González had to shoot that same type of scene repeatedly throughout filming.
“Eiza trained her a** off, and she got in incredible shape for this film. I just have so much respect for her,” he praised.
“Iron Jane,” which marks Sklenar’s first producer credit under his Vista Lane Pictures banner, is expected to debut at festivals next year.

title: Frankie Muniz Hospitalized After Race Car Incident During Daytona Practice
summary: Frankie Muniz was taken to the hospital after he was involved in an incident during a practice at Daytona International Speedway.
story: Frankie Muniz, actor-turned-race-car-driver, was hospitalized on Wednesday, Nov. 11, after an “incident” while practicing at the Daytona International Speedway.
His NASCAR team, Team Reaume, shared the news on Instagram, noting that he was taken to a medical facility to receive care.

“Frankie Muniz was involved in an incident while practicing for today’s Proud to Honor event at Daytona International Speedway,” the statement reads. “He was taken to a local medical facility for further evaluation and is awake and alert.”
“We’ll share updates as they become available,” the statement continued, thanking people for their support. They also asked to respect Muniz’s privacy at this time.

Muniz, best known for his roles in “Malcolm in the Middle” and “Agent Cody Banks,” has been racing for over 20 years. Currently competing in the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series, he was going to be participating in the Ford Proud to Honor Veterans Classic at Daytona Wednesday evening.

Muniz, 40, has been vocal about the struggles he’s faced this year. Back in July, he announced that he and wife Paige Price Muniz were divorcing after 10 years together. The two share 5-year-old son Mauz. The actor, however, removed his original post after receiving backlash from people. The announcement featured both of them dancing with the son and noted, “Who says you can’t stay best friends with your baby momma?”
His estranged wife would go on to defend him, according to People, saying sorry that he felt the need to remove the video because “people are so cruel to you.”
In September, he posted a lengthy post about experiencing a “heavy” time in his life.

“The last 6 weeks of my life have been a nightmare I’m praying to wake up from. Everything felt heavy, unclear, and like it was falling apart at the same time. I wouldn’t wish this season on anyone,” he wrote on X. “The unexpected gift in the middle of it is that I’ve had nowhere to hide. I’ve had time to sit with myself, do real self-reflection, and finally see the areas of my life that need work if I want to become a better version of me. Not the polished version I show the world...the actual one.”
He added, in part, that he was committed to “doing the work” and choosing to treat this chapter of his life as “the foundation, not the finish line.”

title: Amanda Seyfried on ‘You Can See Everything’ Scene With Billy Evans: ‘There Was No Reason for Him to Get That Aggressive’
summary: Among the most tension-filled moments of A24’s bombshell documentary “You Can See Everything,” about disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, is the contentious dinner exchange between Amanda Seyfried and Holmes’ partner, Billy Evans.
story: Among the most tension-filled moments of A24’s bombshell documentary “You Can See Everything,” about disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, is the contentious dinner exchange between Amanda Seyfried and Holmes’ partner, Billy Evans.
Nearly a month after the movie’s premiere, Seyfried is finally opening up about it.

The actor joined co-directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim for a conversation published by Rolling Stone magazine Nov. 11, in which the trio discussed her surprise appearance in the documentary.

In it, Seyfried — who had previously portrayed Holmes in Hulu series “The Dropout” and reprised the role for several scenes in the documentary — had the opportunity to chat with Evans in his home for a meal that quickly devolved into an near-explosive argument.

“There was no reason for him to get that aggressive. (Pauses.) That’s the word I’m going to use, as it’s more diplomatic,” she said in the Rolling Stone interview, her first extensive comments about the film. “If my jaw wasn’t obviously on the floor, you could tell, like, it had come unhinged.”
Evans did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment.

The film, released Oct. 16, documents the family life of Holmes and Evans before and during the tech founder’s prison sentence. Holmes, who reported to the Bryan, Texas federal prison camp in May 2023, had been convicted of fraud. It was only after the film’s release that Seyfried’s involvement was revealed.

In the film, Seyfried is featured in several scenes, drawing on her past experiences, studying the once-promising tech leader’s mannerisms and movements to help Fielder analyze Holmes’ behavior in footage. Because Holmes is behind bars for much of the making of the film, Seyfried ends up stepping into the Theranos founder’s shoes for several reenactments.

Things hit a fever pitch when Seyfried and Fielder visit Evans’ Texas house while Holmes is in prison. It’s during this visit that he reveals he has been impersonating Holmes on her social media accounts. Seyfried, who immediately expresses her opposition to what she perceives as Evans’ controlling behavior, gets into a heated argument with him over dinner.

In their conversation in Rolling Stone, Seyfried told the filmmakers that she went into the conversation with Evans, “honestly trying to connect.” She also mentioned that she was aware his kids, whom he shares with Holmes, were in the house and that she wanted to be open-minded.

“We were all sitting there eating really good Chinese food, and, obviously, there were questions we wanted to ask. But for me, since I’m not an interviewer or an investigator, I’m not so good at asking questions and getting the timing right. And Nathan, you had a rapport with him. I was still creating this rapport.”
Seyfried told Fielder and Oppenheim that her mindset shifted, however, as the meal went on.
“I don’t want to provoke him, but at this point, it’s kind of like, the gloves are off. Because this guy has disrespected me in such a way that I was like, ‘Oh, I don’t think so, buddy,’” she said.

“I was in the frame of mind where I’m like, ‘OK, this guy is disrespectful, and I’m here in his home, I’m gonna argue this because I actually have a pretty solid stance on things. I don’t like the way he’s using this human being, his wife — the person he says he’s ‘building monuments of love’ to — as a tool. Maybe he does respect her, but he’s behaving like he does not respect her.’”
The actor added that she was attempting to be “protective” of herself while also “maintaining some kind of rapport with him, so I can stay and he doesn’t kick us out, you know?”
Seyfried revealed in the same interview that she had wanted to meet Evans after seeing the documentary footage of him and getting “such strong negative feelings from him.”
“I felt like I needed to meet this guy,” she said. “It was exciting to me, and it was scary, and it was questionable.”
The chat with Evans did little to change her opinion of him. In fact, Seyfried told the outlet, it “only got worse.”

Seyfried also spoke to the filmmakers about the unplanned call that Evans got from Holmes herself while they were at his house. It was during that call that she and Fielder had the opportunity to speak to Holmes, who was in prison. As Seyfried tells it, the moment was shocking.

“We didn’t know she was gonna call right then. And I am sitting there with her children and cuddling with her dog! While she’s in prison!” Seyfried said. “And then she calls, and … someone asked me if that was real, if that was really her on the phone. And I’m like, ‘It’s a documentary. Who else would it be?’”
The actor was mum about the entire project, even after its release. When asked about her thoughts on the Holmes-centered documentary in October, Seyfried brushed off the question.
“It’s interesting, yeah, it’s interesting,” she told the Hollywood Reporter.

title: Sheinelle Jones Has ‘Pinch-Me’ Moment With Debbie Allen Reflecting on Her Legacy, Perseverance
summary: Sheinelle Jones spoke with Debbie Allen after the two were recently honored at the 2026 Ebony Power 100 Gala.
story: Sheinelle Jones’ childhood dream came true when she was able to sit down with Debbie Allen to discuss her decades-long illustrious career and recent honor from Ebony magazine.

Both the TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle co-host and the icon were among the inspirational figures in the Black community honored at the 2026 Ebony Power 100 Gala, which was held at the Hollywood Palladium in Los Angeles on Nov. 9.

“It was a night to celebrate excellence in all fields from media and the arts, to trailblazers in science … we’re all just trying to be the best versions of ourselves while paving the way for those coming behind us,” Sheinelle said of the event on Instagram Nov. 10.
After being recognized for their contributions to the culture, Sheinelle sat down with Allen and shared why she has been her “personal hero” for decades.

“I have to let you know how special this moment is for me. The viewers will know of the show because I’ve talked about it so many times. I used to have a cabbage patch. Her name was Lily Debbie Allen,” Sheinelle said.
“Wow, that is so loving,” Allen replied. “Thank you.”
During the Nov. 11 episode of TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle, she reflected on the special moment of being honored alongside one of her childhood heroes.

“From the moment I arrived, I could feel the energy,” Sheinelle said. “There was so much joy, so much history and so much greatness, and I had my own pinch-me moment sitting down with fellow honoree, dancer, choreographer and just legend, Debbie Allen.”

The two chatted about the multi-hyphenate breaking down racial barriers from a young age to pursue her dream, becoming the first Black dance student at the Houston Ballet at age 14. Later, she was rejected from a university program due to her body type. But her mom, Vivian Ayers Allen, wouldn’t let her throw a “pity party” and encouraged her to keep dancing.
“What’s it like for you then in this seat now, to look back and reflect a message that you would want to give others? What would you say?” Sheinelle asked.
“I would say look in the mirror, know who’s looking back, get into that blood memory DNA, and believe in yourself,” Allen said.
“I’m one who has basically made dreams come true. I worked,” she added.

The Ebony Power 100 list features leaders, visionaries and changemakers. Sheinelle was named a “media maven” for joining TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle in January and becoming a New York Times best-selling author with her literary debut, “Through Mom’s Eyes.”

Allen was named one of the Artists in Residence, who “through theater, dance, art, photography and literature have altered culture as we see it today,” according to the magazine. Her accolades include choreographing for Michael Jackson and Dolly Parton, directing episodes of “Scandal,” starring in “Grey’s Anatomy” and founding her nonprofit, the Debbie Allen Dance Academy.

She also produced and directed “A Different World” and was an executive producer for the 2026 Netflix reboot. A devoted fan of the show, Sheinelle revealed that several months ago, she bought a T-shirt printed with Debbie Allen’s 1992 Jet magazine cover on the front. She later gave that shirt to Maleah Joi Moon, star of Netflix’s “A Different World,” on TODAY for her birthday.
“I love this so much,” Allen said.

Speaking about the significance of making the Ebony Power 100 list, Allen pointed out the legacy of the magazine and Johnson Publishing Company, which was founded in 1942 and launched Ebony three years later.
“People around the world were reading these magazines and seeing these pictures, and wanting to channel themselves into it, wanting to share who we are, wanting to be who we are,” she said.
The 2026 Ebony Power 100 honorees also include WNBA star Flau’jae Johnson, food critic Keith Lee, filmmaker Lena Waithe, businessman Byron Allen, musician Brandy and astronaut Victor Glover.

title: Jenna Bush Hager Announces a One-Night-Only Event with ‘Theo of Golden’ Author Allen Levi in Columbus, Georgia
summary: Jenna Bush Hager is headed to Columbus, Georgia with Allen Levi. Here is information for the Read With Jenna live event.
story: Jenna Bush Hager is headed on a literary vacation, and you’re invited!
TODAY’s resident book maven will be in conversation with Allen Levi, author of the publishing phenomenon “Theo of Golden,” for a one-night-only event in Columbus, Georgia.
“We are taking a book vacation to Georgia and we hope you all will come with us,” Jenna said. “I can’t wait to be with Allen in the town that inspired this bestselling book.”
The book is set in an idyllic town called Golden, which is based on Columbus, the city where Levi grew up. Jenna and Allen’s conversation is sponsored by VisitColumbusGA.
Self-published in 2023, “Theo of Golden” was later acquired by Atria Books and has sold 4 million copies in the U.S.
The book follows a contemplative and mysterious older man who moves to a small Georgia town and begins to connect with locals through their portraits.
“It’s a beautiful story of redemption, forgiveness and hope,” according to Jenna.
