title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented  meeting on the sidelines of APEC, officials say
summary: President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen, China’s tech hub, next week, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers.
story: President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen, China’s tech hub, next week, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers.

“President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the president of the United States, the president of the People’s Republic of China and the president of the Russian Federation,” Olivia Wales, a White House spokesperson, said in a call with reporters Friday night. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous.”

It is not anticipated that any sort of agreement will come from the trilateral meeting, according to a senior U.S. official, who described the session as an “entry point” and “the first conversation,” pointing to the reduction of nuclear arsenals as a key topic.

“We do think it’s time for China to sort of step up, you know, to the adults’ table, if you will, and have adult conversations about adult things,” the senior U.S. official said about the issue of nuclear weapons.

Beijing’s arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the U.S. and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With U.S. and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.

The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernized” deal that includes China.
The three-way summit with Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin comes at a complicated moment in relations for the three countries.

Trump intends to discuss the Iran war with the two leaders, but not the war in Ukraine, according to a senior U.S. official, who noted that discussions about the war in Ukraine are a separate “track” that China is not part of so it would not be “appropriate.”

Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the U.S. war with Iran and other tensions between the world’s foremost economic powers.

Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin, even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly 5-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.
There is no bilateral with Putin scheduled, but the two leaders will appear at events and the trilateral meeting together, according to a senior U.S. official.
There are no plans for Trump to engage with North Korea during the trip, according to a senior U.S. official.

Separately, Elon Musk will be the only business leader who is part of the president’s delegation, according to a senior U.S. official, who noted that other U.S. business leaders will attend the summit in their own capacity but there is no official U.S. business delegation.
Musk will not be part of any official meetings, according to a senior U.S. official.

Two senior U.S. officials said that they don’t think Trump will raise the espionage investigation focused on Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence agent who allegedly had a romantic relationship with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, with China.

“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip. In all of our discussions and negotiations with the Chinese, we do not negotiate American export controls,” a senior U.S. official said. “These are national security matters that we develop in the administration and interagency process, and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there.”
Beijing was least certain about the value of the summit
By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China’s growing clout and prestige.
For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.
For Subscribers

“I think the key for Putin was that this was very much about signaling a desire to talk to the president and talk to Chairman Xi in a way that suggests that they’re making decisions on Ukraine, which obviously the Ukrainians and the Europeans don’t like,” said Edgard Kagan, a former U.S. ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
For Subscribers

The trilateral could very well overshadow the APEC summit. The summit, which is bringing 21 economies to Shenzhen, marks a big moment for China to show off its fast-growing, ultramodern coastal metropolis that transformed from a small fishing village into a global technology and economic hub in just a few decades.

More substantively, such a gathering could also muddy China’s argument that a Cold War mentality in the West was a contributing factor that led to Russia’s war on Ukraine and its pointed criticism that the U.S. has undermined international institutions and treaties with how it has executed its war against Iran.

The trilateral meeting could undercut China’s push to portray itself as a defender of free trade at APEC, said Hoo Tiang Boon, a professor of Chinese foreign policy at Nanyang Technological University.
“You sort of run counter to Chinese support of multilateralism,” he said.
The leaders have met in pairs plenty of times over the years
Putin and Xi are no strangers. They’ve fostered a close personal relationship, meeting more than 40 times since Xi became president in 2013 and addressing each other as “dear friend.”

Trump and Putin have met face-to-face on seven different occasions, most recently in Alaska in August 2025. Xi and Trump have held face-to-face talks on eight occasions, including a September state visit to Washington by Xi.
Beijing is the No. 1 trading partner for Moscow, a relationship that has strengthened since Putin sent troops into Ukraine in 2022.

As the EU and the West sought to economically isolate Russia, China increased its purchases of Russia’s energy resources and became Moscow’s principal supplier of key technologies, including high-tech components for Russian weapons industries. Beijing has ignored Western demands to cut those supplies.

In the lead-up to Russia’s war on Ukraine, Xi and Putin declared their countries had a “no-limits friendship.” China officially has said it is neutral on the conflict, while charging that Kyiv’s Western allies played a part in provoking Russia’s military action in Ukraine.
Moscow, in turn, has repeatedly declared its support for Beijing’s policy on issues related to Taiwan.

Trump recently struck a diesel deal with Russia, waiving sanctions against Moscow and allowing for the sale of millions of tons of the fuel. The U.S. leader has blamed surging energy prices on Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries. Analysts, however, say the rise in global crude prices is due mostly to the Iran war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concern that the trilateral meeting could serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv’s back.

Planning for the summit has drawn comparisons to the Yalta Conference, the 1945 gathering at which the leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union agreed to divide Germany and Berlin into four military occupation zones and finalized plans for establishing the United Nations.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has dismissed the Yalta comparisons, noting that any potential agreements reached in Shenzhen can’t be enforced on others.

“It’s clear that a meeting between the leaders of countries such as Russia, China and the United States is extremely significant,” Peskov said. “However, let’s not forget that the vision for a global order is that no one tries to impose any particular view of global order, and it should be based entirely on mutual benefit and mutual respect.”

title: Pope Leo makes emotional return to his ‘beloved diocese of Chiclayo’
summary: Pope Leo XIV made a triumphant return to the Peruvian city of Chiclayo, where he served as bishop for and was affectionately nicknamed “Padre Roberto.”
story: LIMA, Peru — Pope Leo XIV made a triumphant return Friday to the Peruvian city of Chiclayo, where he served as bishop for eight years and was affectionately nicknamed “Padre Roberto.”

Leo arrived in a plane decorated with “#LeoXFliesHome” stickers and he was greeted with a sign at the airport bearing the same message. A small dance troupe performed before him as he stepped onto the tarmac.
He will stay in the area until Sunday to lead eight events, including a private dinner with the priests who once reported to him as bishop.
The crowds greeting Leo in Peru’s fourth-largest city were smaller than the estimated 3 million or so who welcomed the pope when he arrived Wednesday in Lima, the country’s capital.
The Vatican estimated that 1 million people had lined the motorcade route to the Mass and that 500,000 attended.

title: Microsoft services hit by major outage across the world
summary: A widespread outage continued to hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Friday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts.
story: A massive global outage impacting more than a dozen Microsoft cloud services, including Outlook email and Teams messaging stretched into Friday as the tech giant struggled to restore the service, which is critical to the day-to-day functions of governments, schools and businesses around the world.

Starting around 12:50 p.m. ET Thursday, Microsoft began warning users of its products on social media that it was “investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online,” its cloud email service.
By the time workers were arriving at the office on Friday morning, Microsoft said it was still working on the problem.

Microsoft said in its latest update about 7 a.m. ET that it was seeing “encouraging recovery progress in Europe, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected Microsoft 365 infrastructure. “
It added that “North America is also improving; however, some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue.”
Hours earlier the tech giant had warned that attempts “to improve serviceability” were “not taking as expected,” it said in an update on X overnight.
Some on the social media platform derided the technical responses, or hoped email would be down Friday for a possible day off.
There are few products as pervasive inside global companies as Outlook email.
Email traffic to many of the tech giant’s 450 million users came to a halt around midday, with email programs freezing and crashing, and mobile devices unable to refresh inboxes or send messages.

The problems also affected Microsoft’s non-commercial consumer products, according to a notice on its website. “This issue impacts Outlook.com, OneDrive, OneNote To Do, Teams, and Microsoft 365 for the web.”

Throughout the day the problems spread. As of 11 p.m. ET on Thursday, Microsoft’s online status pages said its corporate services Exchange Online, Copilot, Microsoft Planner, Sharepoint, Microsoft To Do, Windows 365, cloud printing services, and mobile device management programs were all experiencing issues.

The problem caused chaos in workplaces around the world. At one, truck manufacturer Workhouse Group, it forced the company to delay its earnings report which was set to be released on Thursday afternoon.
In a statement, Workhorse said: “The rescheduling is due to business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outages taking place today.”

The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner’s Office, the L.A. County Sheriff’s Department and other government agencies in California said their communications were impacted by the outage, NBC Los Angeles reported. In Washington, email services at federal agencies and on Capitol Hill were impacted.

In Colorado, the Arapahoe County Sheriff’s Office said the outage was affecting online bond payments for people being held in its detention facility. “Until Outlook email is restored, anyone needing to post bond for immediate release must do so in person at the jail,” it said on social media.

Throughout most of the day, Microsoft has said it has been working on the issue. By 2:50 p.m. ET, the company wrote on social media that it was “testing a configuration change” to its cloud servers in order to try to restore services.
By 4:40 p.m. ET, the company said it was restarting “affected servers to return them to service.”
Microsoft explained a few minutes later in another post on X that a “core process on affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, causing capacity loss.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The company also said it was “shifting traffic” around in order to relieve overwhelmed servers that remained online.

But then not long after, the company again said, “The servers we returned to service can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic; we’re analyzing diagnostic data to determine what’s triggering the behavior.”

The updates continued into the night. At 11:36 p.m., Microsoft said it its efforts to improve server stability were ongoing, but that while it was “observing partial recovery across regions in which we’ve applied these adjustments” that didn’t result in “sustained recovery.”

NBC News attempted to reach Microsoft representatives through multiple phone numbers listed on the company’s press releases and through a phone number to its investor relations department, however the company has not commented in response.

An email sent to a public relations firm that represents Microsoft from a personal non-Outlook or Microsoft based email address quickly bounced back, with an error message reading that the server was “unavailable or unable to receive mail.”
In a statement to Bloomberg News, a Microsoft spokesperson said: “We appreciate our customers’ patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible.”

Major outages, such as Microsoft’s, are not unprecedented but have become increasingly rare. In 2024, a glitch with a security program led to Windows devices around the world freezing, causing them displaying Microsoft’s well-known “blue screen of death” error. That issue brought airlines, companies, and critical systems to a halt.
Some of Microsoft’s other critical cloud services, such as its Azure cloud computing platform, that powers many websites and apps, remained online and did not have any additional issues.

title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills at least six people, officials say
summary: An Israeli airstrike on a hospital in southern Gaza overnight killed at least six people, the Health Ministry in the Palestinian enclave said Thursday.
story: An Israeli airstrike on a hospital in southern Gaza overnight killed at least six people, the Health Ministry in the Palestinian enclave said Thursday.

The strike hit a surgery building at Nasser Hospital, with medical staff and patients among those killed, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy, health officials said. The Israeli military said it was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants.

The strike — the latest despite an ongoing U.S.-backed ceasefire — shattered ceilings and left debris strewn across wards inside the hospital, which is one of the few functioning medical facilities left in Gaza after the destruction of Israel’s yearslong military assault.

Palestinian surgeon Dr. Rizk Abu Shaira was among those killed, the Health Ministry said. He was featured in the 2026 documentary “American Doctor,” which followed three American doctors helping to provide medical care in Gaza.

title: Ukraine faces new Starshield disruptions as Trump envoys meet with Putin
summary: Hours after an American delegation touched down in Moscow for peace talks, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country’s military had experienced a renewed wave of “significant disruptions” to the Starshield satellite internet service, hampering its ability to defend itself against Russia.
story: Hours after an American delegation touched down in Moscow for peace talks, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country’s military had experienced a renewed wave of “significant disruptions” to the Starshield satellite internet service, hampering its ability to defend itself against Russia.
“These are not random errors but systematic speed restrictions,” he said in a Telegram post. “For us, this primarily means a significant complication in intercepting Russian jet-powered drones.”

His comments came as U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, arrived in the Russian capital for peace talks with President Vladimir Putin, a day after trilateral talks aimed at ending the war were held in the United Arab Emirates.
The two-day Abu Dhabi summit, the first such meeting since February, ended with no major breakthrough, although representatives of Russia and Ukraine agreed on a large exchange of prisoners of war.
In Moscow, Kushner told ‌Putin that Europe wanted ‌a role ‌in future negotiations, according to Russia’s Tass state news agency.

European countries cut communications with the Kremlin and refused to engage with Russia directly after Putin launched his invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, but have since expressed concern about the Trump administration’s softening stance toward the Kremlin. Kushner last week said he also wanted to address “long-term European security and stability,” signaling a focus beyond just Ukraine that prompted a firm response from European leaders.

Expanding on that theme on Thursday, Kushner said there was a “very strong momentum and desire” from European leaders to “engage together,” adding that “understanding the long-term security between Russia, Ukraine, and Europe is a conversation that we started having with them.”

While representatives from several European countries were in Abu Dhabi, they did not play a direct role in the talks. Russian negotiators have previously opposed their involvement, citing Europe’s support for Kyiv as an obstacle.

At the meeting in Moscow, the Interfax news agency reported that Putin proposed a joint Russian-Ukrainian humanitarian mission to the city of Kostiantynivka ⁠in eastern ​Ukraine, similar to the Melania Trump-brokered mission in Oleshky that allowed residents to leave the Russian-controlled town.
Thursday’s talks were “substantive, constructive, frank and useful,” Putin’s aide Yuri Ushakov said.
Kushner and Witkoff met with Putin for about two hours before going to Dublin, where they met with Zelenskyy for more than an hour as the conflict stretches toward the five-year mark.

Zelenskyy in Dublin indicated the Europeans would not be on the sidelines. “Next meeting, Europe will be during negotiations, will be a negotiation team — not some way, not separately. They will have a voice,” he said.
The U.S. and Zelenskyy want Europe to appoint a single person to negotiate with Moscow.
Zelenskyy also said Thursday that military units had for several days reported internet speed restrictions affecting the entire front line and Russian-occupied parts of the country.

A limit of 100 mph is once again being “imposed on Starshield,” he said of the military version of SpaceX’s Starlink communications service. The system normally runs at a stable speed exceeding around 250 mph.
“These are not random errors but systematic speed restrictions,” he said. “For us, this primarily means a significant complication in intercepting Russian jet-powered drones.”
“Unfortunately, there have already been strikes that got through because our interception systems cannot reach sufficient speeds and are unable to intercept in time,” he added.
Zelenskyy added that Ukraine was trying to ⁠clarify the reasons for the ‌restriction with the ​U.S. side.
SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment from NBC News.

Craig Albert, the graduate director of national defense studies at Augusta University, said decreasing Starshield’s speed would slow down how fast Ukraine’s offensive drones travel, “which makes them pretty much target practice for faster interceptor drones by the Russians.”
It would also slow down Ukrainian interceptor drones and their missile defense systems, meaning “Russian drones can get through their defenses much quicker.”

“The Russians can target more infrastructure, and the Ukrainians just don’t have the speed to counteract,” he said, adding that “for the price, the scale, the speed, the scalability, and the efficiency,” there were no real options other than Starshield.
Ukraine first raised the alarm last month about speed limits being imposed on Starshield, which is crucial to its battlefield operations and air defenses.

Starlink owner Elon Musk initially put the responsibility for the restrictions on Trump, who has been trying to pressure Kyiv to make concessions to end the war. The U.S. government said ​that any such decision could only have been ‌made by Musk.

Trump denied being involved in the decision concerning the slowdown. Musk later said in an X post that SpaceX had acted to close a “loophole” with its civilian Starlink service, accusing Ukraine of violating “Starlink terms of service” by using it for offensive drone strikes, which the country denied.
Moscow has so far resisted such efforts to bring Europe to the main negotiating table, something Ukraine has long sought.
The talks came against the backdrop of continued fighting on the front lines, where neither side has achieved significant progress for months.

Instead, the focus has shifted to daily attacks with long-range missiles and drones. Russia has targeted Ukrainian cities, aiming to cut off water and power supplies as winter sets in. Kyiv has resumed attacks on energy infrastructure, a campaign that drew Trump’s ire.
Ukrainian officials said Thursday that five civilians had been killed by Russian strikes on the country overnight, and 29 people injured. The Russian Defense Ministry said it had shot down 71 drones.

title: Megaspeed, chip firm at center of Nvidia scandal, pledges to cooperate with U.S. investigation
summary: HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the tech company at the center of the Chinese spy scandal that engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said Thursday it will cooperate with the U.S. government’s investigations into the matter.
story: HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the tech company at the center of the Chinese spy scandal that engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said Thursday it will cooperate with the U.S. government’s investigations into the matter.

Megaspeed’s statement came hours before the resignation of Huang, one of the leaders of the AI boom, who co-founded the American chipmaker and helped build it into the world’s second most valuable company.

In its first statement since reports emerged about Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the future of the tech giant, Megaspeed said that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.”
U.S. intelligence agencies determined that Alice Huang had an affair with the Nvidia CEO and was a Chinese intelligence operative, a person with knowledge of the matter told NBC News on Sunday.

She held a senior position at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that was one of Nvidia’s biggest customers in Southeast Asia. Megaspeed is under U.S. criminal investigation for allegedly smuggling American-made chips into China in defiance of U.S. export controls.

A criminal investigation is ongoing in Singapore, where officials said Thursday Alice Huang had been barred from re-entering the country. The government also issued her with a stern warning after finding that she had knowingly provided police with inaccurate information to downplay her role in the company. It said that Huang was not investigated for espionage.

The country’s Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement that authorities had interviewed Huang and impounded her passport in 2025, but that its requests for cooperation from U.S. authorities had gone unanswered.
“Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company,” it said.

Investigators concluded in February that there was “insufficient evidence to establish that Huang had committed any offences,” the statement said, adding that investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals were continuing, related to the shipment of servers via Singapore.

Megaspeed, meanwhile, said in the statement Thursday that it has “cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and stands ready to cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority.” The statement was signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan.
It said that “Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government.”

China has dismissed the spying allegations as “smears.” On Thursday, a Foreign Ministry spokesperson said that “the U.S. side should stop fabricating so-called espionage narratives as a pretext for implementing technological blockades.”

Megaspeed did not address the allegations surrounding Alice Huang, but said that “to further reinforce our commitment to compliance, Megaspeed has retained a leading U.S. law firm to lead a comprehensive census of its graphics processing units (GPUs) and independently verify its export control compliance practices.”

The company added that it “welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws.”
Nvidia’s stock price has plunged since its 63-year-old chief admitted over the weekend to being “unfaithful” to his wife.

Huang quit on Thursday in the wake of reports that he had multiple extramarital relationships. In a statement, Nvidia named its executive vice president and chief financial officer Colette Kress as its interim CEO.
Nvidia’s board met Wednesday night to address Huang’s future at the company, a source familiar with the matter told NBC News, adding that the White House was aware of the meeting.
The scandal has raised questions about how much U.S. government officials knew about Alice Huang and Megaspeed.

In the spring, Secretary of State Marco Rubio circulated a memo to officials in the Trump administration outlining how U.S. intelligence showed that the Nvidia CEO was in a romantic relationship with a business executive who was an asset of China’s spy service, according to a person familiar with Nvidia and a former national security official with knowledge of the matter. The New York Times and the Financial Times first reported on this memo.

Alice Huang’s precise role and relationship with China’s spy service remain unclear, however. It’s possible she was not a career spy for China’s spy agency, the Ministry of State Security, but was asked to cooperate and share information based on her access to Huang, a former national security official with knowledge of the matter told NBC News.
Rep. Jim Himes, D-Conn., ranking Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, told NPR that Alice Huang’s role still needed to be clarified.
Democrats will soon hold control of both the House and the Senate and, as a result, will have subpoena power.

On Wednesday night, as the Nvidia board met, Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Chris Coons, D-Del., announced they had written to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick with a request to preserve records on the subject.

title: U.S. charges 3 men with plotting multiple terror attacks, including on British air base
summary: One of the men helped direct the planned attack against the air base while he was in a U.S. prison, according to a Justice Department indictment.
story: Three men, including one already jailed in the U.S., were accused by U.S. authorities Tuesday of being Iran-supported operatives who plotted nearly 20 attacks on Jewish communities in Europe and the U.S., as well as a planned assault on a British air base used by the U.S. Air Force.

Charges against Mohammad Al-Saadi, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national; Mohsen Mohajeri, an Iranian national; and Mohammad Ali Al-Hassani, an Iraqi national, were outlined in a superseding indictment unsealed in federal court in New York City.
Only Al-Saadi — an alleged pro-Iranian terrorist who is believed to have plotted attacks across Europe, Canada and the U.S., as first reported by NBC News — is in custody.

U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald in New York said in a news release that Al-Saadi, who was arrested in the spring, continued to coordinate with his co-defendants in the days leading up to the attempted September terrorist plot at a British Royal Air Force Base in Fairford, where U.S. bombers and troops had been stationed.

“As alleged, these defendants helped orchestrate a campaign of terror on behalf of terrorist organizations affiliated with Iran that targeted Jewish communities in Europe and the United States, and the British military base, RAF Fairford, housing American service members,” said McDonald, whose office is handling the case.
“The threat presented by Iran and Iran-backed terrorist groups to America and our allies is not hypothetical — it is very real,” he added in the statement.

The new indictment offers fresh insight into an episode that has been shrouded in mystery for more than a month after five men were detained after midnight Sept. 27 on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offenses after three suspicious vans were spotted traveling toward the base in western England.

The Justice Department indictment alleges that Al-Hassani paid associates to carry out surveillance of RAF Fairford in August and paid several people to move forward with the plot in September “by procuring vans and barrels of fuel, researching the purchase of chemical accelerants, including large quantities of potassium chloride, and purchasing metallic objects that could be used as explosive shrapnel.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The group even made custom decals to give the vans the appearance that they were used by a fuel company and a swimming pool supply business, authorities say.
Al-Hassani is alleged to have then tasked the people to go to the base with the fuel when U.K. law enforcement took the men into custody.

Al-Saadi was helping direct the RAF Fairford plot while he was in a U.S. prison, according to the indictment. He made video and phone calls to his family members in Iraq, who are alleged to have passed coded messages to Al-Hassani and Mohajeri.
In a July call with his sister, Al-Saadi asked, “What are we doing about all our old work?” — a reference to terrorist activity — according to investigators.
His sister replied, “It isn’t cancelled,” investigators said.
In June, Al-Saadi pleaded not guilty to charges that he plotted at least 18 attacks in Europe in retaliation for the U.S. and Israel’s war with Iran.

But the indictment alleges that the three men conspired to use a network of contacts in the United Kingdom to commit terrorist attacks on behalf of an Iran-aligned terrorist network, which included Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and Kata’ib Hizballah.

The European attacks “were carried out in the name of a purportedly new terrorist group with the pseudonym Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (“HAYI”), which is actually a front for Kata’ib Hizballah,” the release said.
The U.S. government has designated Kata’ib Hizballah and the Revolutionary Guards as foreign terrorist organizations.

title: Senior U.S. Army soldier arrested in U.K. on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence
summary: The 41-year-old man was arrested “as part of an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing” near the ⁠city of Gloucester, ​in the west ⁠of England, British police said.
story: LONDON — A senior U.S. Army soldier was arrested in the U.K. on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence, British police said Tuesday.

The 41-year-old man was arrested “as part of an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing” near the ⁠city of Gloucester, ​in the west ⁠of England, London’s Metropolitan Police said in a statement, adding that he remained in custody at a police station in London.

He was ​arrested ⁠on suspicion of ‌offenses under sections 1 and 3 of the National Security Act, ‌the statement said. They relate to obtaining ‌or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service.
“The country to which the allegations relate is Russia,” the statement added.

Three people familiar with the matter told NBC News that the soldier was based at NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps headquarters at Imjin Barracks on the outskirts of Gloucester. A senior NATO military official also confirmed the location of the soldier’s assignment.

FBI Director Kash Patel was quoted in the statement as saying that the arrest was “important” and that it “involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies.”
The FBI, he added, “has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners.”

Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, was quoted in the police statement as saying, “The alleged conduct of a senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent.”said.

“This case demonstrates the strength of our partnerships and the resolve of the counterintelligence community,” he added. “I am grateful to the U.K. and the FBI for their professionalism and teamwork throughout this investigation.”
Calling the allegations “very serious,” Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, Britain’s senior national coordinator for counterterrorism policing, said the “investigation is very much ongoing.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The investigation is not linked to any other ongoing counterterrorism operations, the statement said.
The arrest comes at a time of heightened tensions around the threat from hostile states, with British security services saying Russia and Iran have both used proxies to commit crimes on U.K. soil.

Officials in the U.K. have said proxies linked to Iran have been behind a string of arson fires and other attacks in Britain and other countries, many of them targeting the Jewish community and intended to sow fear.
The U.S. has moved military aircraft from an air base in the U.K. amid threats from Iran.
A U.S. official confirmed to NBC News that several military aircraft had left RAF Mildenhall as the security posture there had increased.
At least eight air refueling tankers and three Osprey tilt-rotor military transports left the base in Suffolk, eastern England, on Monday, flight tracking data showed.

title: U.S. moves military aircraft from British base amid Iran threats
summary: A U.S. official confirmed to NBC News that several military aircraft had left RAF Mildenhall as the security posture there had increased.
story: LONDON — The United States has moved military aircraft from an air base in the United Kingdom amid threats from Iran.
A U.S. official confirmed to NBC News that several military aircraft had left RAF Mildenhall as the security posture there had increased.
They were operating under “enhanced force protection measures,” the official said. The official would not speculate on the exact nature of the threat that appears to have led to ramped-up security.
At least eight air refueling tankers and three Osprey tilt-rotor aircraft left the base in Suffolk, eastern England, on Monday, flight tracking data showed.

Some of the tankers, Boeing KC-135 Stratotankers, were relocated to air bases in Germany and Spain, with one moved to the area of Glasgow Prestwick Airport in Scotland. The Ospreys were moved to nearby RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk.

It comes weeks after the U.S. withdrew bombers from another base in Britain, RAF Fairford, after police foiled a suspected terrorist plot linked to Iran. The U.S. has used bases in the U.K. to strike Iran.

The Wall Street Journal, which was first to report on this week’s movements, said the evacuation came following a threat from Iran, citing people familiar with the matter. It said that the exact nature of the threat was not yet known and that it remained under discussion by U.S. officials.
“We take proactive measures to ensure our aircraft, our people and our installations remain safe and secure,” a U.S. official told NBC News.

A U.S. European Command official said: “U.S. Air Force aircraft rotate between installations and operating locations for a variety of reasons including training and real world requirement. U.S. military aircraft are hosted in accordance with access, basing, and overflight agreements with our Allies and partners. Due to operations security, we will not provide further information on movement of assets.”
A spokesperson for the U.K. Defense Ministry said it does “not routinely comment on the activity of other nations.”
“Aircraft and other assets move regularly according to operational requirements,” the spokesperson said.

The U.S. pulled aircraft from RAF Fairford last month following reports of a possible Iranian drone attack, two U.S. officials have told NBC News. That move came in the wake of an investigation into a possible planned terrorist attack at the base, which is in Gloucestershire.
Five men were detained on Sept. 27 after three suspicious vans were spotted traveling toward RAF Fairford. Other arrests followed, and two men were charged under the National Security Act.
The incident, which attracted huge international attention, remains largely unexplained, although British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the activity was likely to have been coordinated in Iran.

Though Tehran has denied involvement in any plot against RAF Fairford, its powerful Revolutionary Guard warned in July that any base used to launch attacks against Iranian territory was a legitimate target.
Iran has vowed to retaliate for any renewal of the American-Israeli war against it and has threatened to expand its response beyond the Middle East.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday that Washington had addressed concerns about reported threats from Tehran against American diplomats overseas by “moving people away from the threat.”

“Obviously, we’re always worried about the safety and security of our personnel and their families overseas,” Rubio said. “And so, when we see anything that could pose a potential threat beyond a certain threshold, we’re going to address it.”
Citing new “momentum” in negotiations to end the war, President Donald Trump downplayed the prospect of new U.S. attacks Monday.
“Iran militarily is effectively over,” Trump said after a meeting with Qatar’s prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani.
Further U.S. attacks “won’t be necessary” at this point, but Washington remains “locked and loaded” should circumstances change, Trump told reporters at the White House.

title: Nvidia opens investigation after CEO’s affair with alleged Chinese spy
summary: Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in an employee memo. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.
story: Nvidia’s board of directors said Sunday that it is opening an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

The announcement followed recent reporting by The New York Times and the Financial Times about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who the newspapers reported had been recruited to spy for China. The two are not related.
A person familiar with the matter told NBC News late Sunday that U.S. intelligence agencies had determined that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy and had a relationship with Nvidia’s Jensen Huang.

“The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort,” the company said in a statement.

“A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.”
The company added that while it “has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information.”
In a memo to Nvidia employees that the company shared with NBC News, Huang said: “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.”

The New York Times and the Financial Times reported that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen whose Singapore-based company was buying Nvidia’s advanced chips, had been under surveillance by U.S. intelligence agencies. Those agencies, the reports said, found that she had been recruited to spy by China’s top intelligence agency.
Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday that “the so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China.”

title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assaults
summary: The 51-year-old comedian and actor was found guilty in a British court last week.
story: LONDON — British comedian and actor Russell Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison for rape and sexual assault by a London court Monday.
The lengthy prison term completes a stunning fall from grace for Brand, 51, who found fame on both sides of the Atlantic chronicling his promiscuity and battles with addiction.
He was found guilty Thursday of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He had pleaded not guilty to all counts and denied all of the allegations.

Brand appeared in the London court Monday wearing a dark suit and at times making a sign of the cross as the judge, Justice Joel Bennathan, called him a “sexual predator” before he delivered the sentence. Bennathan had warned last week that Brand faced a “significant” prison term for his crimes.
Stressing that he had to be careful not to punish Brand more “because you are famous,” Bennathan also paid tribute to the “determination and bravery” of the women who testified against him.

“Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent,” he added.
According to Britain’s sentencing council, the maximum sentence for rape is life imprisonment and 10 years for one count of sexual assault.
Brand’s victims told the court Monday — in person and in written statements — that they were still living with the trauma and effects in their daily lives.

“I’ve been in shock and turmoil for years,” a woman told the sentencing hearing, while another said he appeared to show “no remorse.” Victims of alleged sexual offenses are granted anonymity for life under British law.
London’s Metropolitan Police said it had provided prosecutors with investigations into two more rape allegations against Brand since he was convicted.

Asked by reporters whether he had a message for the victims as he left court, Brand’s father, Ron Brand, said he didn’t care about them and suggested they had “chased and harassed” his son. He added that he didn’t believe in the justice system “on the basis of what I just watched.”
Brand’s case has renewed scrutiny of the ethics of the entertainment industry, through which Brand rose from a flamboyant British broadcaster and stand-up comedian to a star of Hollywood movies.

title: Gunman with far-right views who killed 6 in Poland shooting rampage dies in hospital
summary: The man, described as being his mid-20s, was shot by police during Saturday’s attack in the main square of Poland’s second-largest city.
story: The man who killed six people and wounded 15 others in a suspected far-right terrorist attack in the Polish city of Kraków has died, police said early Monday.
Michał Oksiński, 24, died at 4:30 a.m. local time (10:30 p.m. ET), authorities said. He had been in critical condition since the attack and had undergone several operations.
Police shot Oksiński during Saturday’s midday rampage in Main Market Square, the historic center and major tourist destination in Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city.
Four women and two men were killed. Three of the women and one of the men were Polish, authorities said. A British man and an Austrian woman were among the dead, they said.

Two police officers were in “serious” condition after they were injured along with dozens of others, regional official Krzysztof Jan Klęczar said Sunday. Five foreigners, from the U.K., Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria, were injured, officials said.
The bodies of Oksiński’s sister, mother and father were found at the family home in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 90 miles northeast of Kraków, authorities said.

Very little information has come out about Oksiński. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said Saturday that he used an automatic rifle to carry out the attack and that he “was fascinated by far-right ideologies.” The shooter held “very radical” and “ultranationalistic” views, Kierwiński added.
Authorities were still examining the evidence Monday.
The nationalist opposition has questioned the grounds on which the motive was established, with Law & Justice party leader Jarosław Kaczyński saying the claims were a “blatant lie.”
And National Prosecutor’s Office spokesperson Przemyslaw Nowak said at a news conference Monday that investigators did not yet know what motivated the killer.
He said a yellow flag with a snake and the words “Don’t tread on me” on it, known as the Gadsden flag, was found in his room.

First used during the American Revolution in the 18th century, Nowak said, the flag was associated with “various meanings related to freedom or rebellion” but was not widely known as being linked to any form of extremism.
Interior Ministry spokesperson Karolina Galecka said there were many different emblems on the perpetrator’s clothing that had already been partially examined and interpreted.

Separately, government spokesperson Adam Szłapka told Polish broadcaster TVN24 that it was “best to refrain from making comments” about Oksiński’s political views “until the matter is fully clarified and the authorities are in possession of complete information,” even if there were “some initial indications.”
Elsewhere, Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek told Radio Zet that the investigation would continue to establish whether Oksiński acted alone or was inspired by any group.
However, authorities have said they believed the attacker killed his family, possibly while they slept, before he headed to Krakow.

Seven weapons were found in the home, bringing the total recovered to 11, prosecutors said. Four others, including two AR-15 semiautomatic rifles, were found on the attacker or in his car in Kraków. Dozens, if not hundreds, of shots were fired, they said.

However, it has emerged that Oksiński and his father held gun permits and that he had trained at a local shooting club, which said in a statement that he “was never trained in our club in the areas of dynamic, tactical or combat shooting.”

Poland had never experienced such a large mass shooting, and the scenes of bodies and blood strewn across the heart of one of its most historic cities have shocked people in a country that has long viewed itself as safer than its Western European neighbors.

title: Parents, sister of far-right Kraków shooter found dead in family home
summary: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków, Poland, belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.
story: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków, Poland, belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.

Investigators are looking at the deaths of the shooter’s parents and sister as they unravel events surrounding the random violence in the Polish city’s historic center, Main Market Square, around 3 p.m. Saturday.
The relatives, who lived about 90 miles from Kraków, most likely died from gunshot wounds, according to police.
Authorities said the shooter, who survived a shootout with police and remains in the hospital, wore a bulletproof vest.

World leaders paid tribute to victims, and Poland declared two national days of mourning after the shooter, motivated by far-right ideologies killed six people in Kraków in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.”

The dead are a man from the United Kingdom, a woman from Austria and four Polish nationals, according to regional official Krzysztof Jan Klęczar. The injured include visitors from Britain, Portugal, Russia, Germany and Austria, according to The Associated Press.
St. Mary’s Basilica in the square paused its hourly trumpet call overnight in honor of the victims. It was the first time the historic church had done so since World War II.

The gunman, whom officials described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs, is reported to have opened fire in Kraków’s Main Market Square. The midday attack was the country’s deadliest shooting in decades, while a policeman who confronted the gunman is in critical condition.

The suspect is being investigated on suspicion of murder in connection, Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek said Sunday on X, adding that he “acted with the aim of seriously intimidating a large number of people, making this a terrorist offence.”
The same suspect faces a separate murder charge over killings in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyskie, Żurek said, a town 93 miles northeast of Kraków, where three of his relatives were found dead in his home.

“Establishing all the circumstances of these tragic events, determining the full sequence of the perpetrator’s actions and securing evidence are currently the priorities of the investigation,” which is being led by terror offense specialists within the prosecutor’s office, he said.
Kraków prosecutor Eryk Stasielak said that the shooter was in critical condition and that victim autopsies are set to start Monday, according to PAP, a Polish news service.
“Tomorrow we will be deciding the fate of the attacker, if he survives, because he remains in critical condition,” Stasielak said, according to a translation of the report.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński did not name the suspect, identifying him only as a Polish national in his mid-20s from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyskie. He used an automatic rifle, Kierwiński said Saturday, describing him as having “ultranationalistic” views.
“Everything indicates he was fascinated by far-right ideologies,” he said.
The suspect was shot by police at the scene and taken to the hospital around 3 p.m.
A man and two women later found dead in an apartment are believed to be the suspect’s parents and sister, according to Andrzej Fijołek, deputy inspector of Police National Headquarters.
The Interior Ministry announced two national days of mourning Sunday and Monday.

Pope Leo XIV expressed his sadness in a message to the archbishop of Kraków on Sunday. The pope “implores the gift of Christian hope for the families overwhelmed by grief and joins with all those experiencing these days of mourning,” the message read, according to a translation.
Żurek, the justice minister, said early Sunday on social media that Senior Constable Jakub Kulik “is fighting for his life in hospital” after he confronted the shooter.
“One of his lungs is not functioning, and he needs every drop of blood he can get,” he posted on X.
Police later said blood banks in Kraków were full and thanked those who donated.
“Senior constable Jakub Kulik and senior constable Artur Moranski are true heroes,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said, referring to both officers.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Klęczar said that without “the efficient and selfless intervention” of the officers, “the number of victims could have been significantly higher.”
“The condition of the two police officers remains serious,” Klęczar said Sunday. Kierwiński later said the two men had been brought out of comas.

Video on social media shows what appears to be an injured police officer firing at the gunman before he drops to his knees and rolls over onto his back. The officer, who did not appear to have backup nearby, struggles to reload his firearm and appears to be clutching his right arm.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the U.K. government “deeply mourns the British national and other victims” who died.
“The U.K. stands resolutely in solidarity with the people of Poland,” he said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also said Saturday that his country “stands in solidarity” with neighboring Poland, calling the shooting a “shocking crime.”
The U.S. State Department said it was not aware of any American citizens harmed in the violence.
“The profound depth of Poland’s shock at the horror of yesterday’s appalling mass murder in Krakow is truly remarkable to behold,” the U.S. ambassador to Poland, Tom Rose, said in a post on X.

Noting how rare the incident was in an “extraordinarily safe” country like Poland, he added, “There’s something profoundly precious about being in a country where such evil remains so foreign to everyday life, where an entire nation recoils in horror at the mere thought of it, and where the depth of grief reveals the true goodness of its people.”
Part of Main Market Square in Kraków and surrounding streets reopened Sunday, but cordons remain while police carry out forensic work, the city has said in a statement.
Several makeshift memorials with flowers and candles appeared across the city Sunday.
Tourists caught up in attack
Many of those caught up in the attack were tourists visiting the city.

Taylor Dorfmeister, 21, a student from Santa Cruz, California, studying in Italy who was visiting Poland, was in the square with his roommate when gunfire erupted. Dorfmeister said there was a delay before the crowd reacted and then everyone began to flee. He said he took shelter in a building.
“We ran up the stairs in the building to hide, and it was a dead end, which is when I was the most terrified, since the gunshots were [loud] and near,” Dorfmeister told NBC News.
It sounded to Dorfmeister like the gunfire was coming from the first floor of the building where he hid. He was “fully prepared for the worst” based on the proximity of the noise, he said.
“This is it,” Dorfmeister thought. “Like, there’s nowhere to go, nowhere to hide.”
Marie-Ange Collaer was visiting with her family from Brussels.

“We literally ran for our lives and managed to hide from the bullets flying around,” she wrote on Facebook. “Lying on the floor in a shop like in a bad police movie whilst you hear bullets everywhere.”
Collaer said that her family were shaky and “quite in shock” after they returned to their hotel and that everyone was grateful to be alive.
“We saw a few that did not make it, true horror,” she wrote.
U.K. resident Neil Thaxton and his wife, Nicky, also survived the attack.

“We had just walked through the main square and heard the gunshots,” Thaxton wrote on Facebook. “We thought it was fireworks then people started running, we went into a gift shop and the staff took us in the back of the shop and locked the doors and turned the lights off.”
